Report-first; REFUSES exit 1 on a blind derivation or an uncompiled corpus.

**First measurement, clippy 0.1.98 (48a229ceae 2026-09-01):** 822 derived
lints in 9 groups · 54 corpus-covered · **768 UNCOVERED** · **449 of those
fire on a plain `cargo clippy`**. Per-group debt: style 136/158 ·
pedantic 132/143 · restriction 132/132 · complexity 127/143 ·
suspicious 83/83 · correctness 66/67 · nursery 50/53 · perf 37/38 ·
cargo 5/5.

**Two cross-checks nothing had measured, both clean.** `fix-set-only = 0` —
every one of the 51 `FIXABLE ∪ VERIFY` names has a corpus rule, so the
corpus-lockstep law ("no corpus entry without a proposer") holds from the
CONVERSE side, which only the forward direction had ever been asserted for.
And 0 name collisions against the 173 rule ids in the other five compiled
domains (the Batch-146 dedup law) — expected, because those are kebab-case
concept ids, but expected-and-unmeasured is what that law exists for.

⛔ **The finding outranks the candidate list: 0 of the 449 default-firing
uncovered lints carry ANY frequency evidence.** Every evidenced row is
`allow`-level. The mechanism is the evidence's own provenance — the Bench 061
histogram was captured with pedantic+nursery ENABLED over repos this stack
had already clippy-swept, so it ranks the OPT-IN tail and is structurally
blind to the debt an ordinary user sees. Staging off the ranked head alone
therefore stages opt-in lints, deliberately or not. The report prints the
cross-tab and says `⚠ DISJOINT` out loud rather than leaving a reader to
compute it. **The successor lead is a default-level histogram, not another
rule** — filed in `.distill/001` §post-mining intake.

**T3 — the frequency axis joins two cited sources and never estimates.**
Local: the Bench 061 fired histogram with capture date, source-repo count and
dataset digest printed, plus a loud warning that it was captured under cargo
1.97 while the sweep runs 1.98. Study: kornel's published 100K-crate top-10
(`.benchmarks/021`), transcribed WITH counts and restricted to the **3 rows
in the `clippy::` namespace** — the other 7 are rustc lints, and attributing
their frequency to a clippy corpus gap is the transcription error the arm
pins against. **Tier dominates count**: a 2-source row at 90 firings outranks
a 1-source row at 1011, because the two are different populations (6 repos on
one day vs 100K crates) and summing them would invent a third number. A lint
neither source observed renders `uncited`, **not zero**. Li et al. (ICSE
2024) is deliberately NOT transcribed — 021 cites it for the SHAPE of the
distribution, not a per-lint table, and inventing per-lint counts from a
shape claim is what this axis exists to refuse.

`MachineApplicable` is declared **underivable** rather than printed: it is a
property of an EMITTED diagnostic, not of a lint declaration; the
`--clippy-json` oracle lane owns that axis.

## 2026-09-16 — Issues 110 + 111: two silent-wrong-verdict defects, both found by running this crate somewhere it had never been run

### 110 — every scratch crate was ONE cargo unit

All three scratch-crate oracles — `ClippyVerifier` (`clippy_verify`),
`PerfVerifier` (`perf_verify`), `PerfBenchValidator` (`perf_bench`) — BLAKE3-key
the scratch **directory** and wrote a **fixed package name**. Cargo's unit
metadata for a ROOT package does not separate two identically-named ones by
manifest path, so two scratch crates sharing a target dir are one unit and the
second gets the first's cached answer.

Known-answer proof, outside this repo, one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`:

```text
cargo clippy --manifest-path a/…   # "fn f() {}"           Finished 0.20s
cargo clippy --manifest-path b/…   # "no code fence here"  Finished 0.00s, exit 0  ⛔
cargo run    --manifest-path a/…   →  I AM CRATE A
cargo run    --manifest-path b/…   →  I AM CRATE A                              ⛔
```

For `ClippyVerifier` that is `present_lints = []` → `lint_resolved = true`:
**the healer accepts a fix that was never verified.** For `PerfBenchValidator`
it is worse than a wrong verdict — `cargo run` re-executes the other crate's
binary, so the harness times one rule's code and reports the nanoseconds under
another rule's id. A measurement that never happened, reported as one.

Repair: the package name (and, for the bench, the `[[bin]]` name) carries the
BLAKE3 stem, and the probe's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is PINNED to
`<crate_dir>/target` rather than inherited. 3 new arms, none needing a
toolchain — the collision is decided in the manifest, which is why it was
assertable all along. The pre-existing
`prepare_crate_different_code_different_dir` asserted the property that does
*not* matter, which is how this survived in two repos.

⚠ Exposure needs a **shared** target dir, i.e. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set — the
isolated-target idiom this workspace recommends for measuring on a busy box.
**The more carefully somebody isolates a run, the more reliably these oracles
lied to them.**

⛔ Found by riir-train Issue 555, where the same code — a *port* of
`ClippyVerifier` — was a 2-in-3 flake on a bare box and a deterministic red
under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (fixed there at `61d85d62`). The child shed the defect
first; this is the parent catching up. UNDETERMINED and deliberately not
assumed either way: whether any shipped `fix_verify` verdict, corpus label or
`.benchmarks/` perf row was produced under a shared target dir — nothing
recorded the environment.

### 111 — the platform-audit mod-row lattice resolved NOTHING on Windows

`ModRowLattice::build` resolves `#[cfg] mod x;` rows with `Path::join`, which
emits `\` on Windows, against a key set that uses `/` (from `git ls-files`, or
a caller's literal). They never match, so no mod row resolves — and an
unresolved mod row does not error: the lattice degrades to empty,
`files_modrow_gated` reads **0**, every gated item's root context reads as
ungated, and the audit **invents platform-dead findings**. A real walk is
mixed (`E:\repo\src/util/mod.rs`), so normalising one side is not enough; the
index is keyed by the separator-insensitive form and maps back to the original.

**8 of this module's own fixtures were red on clean `HEAD`** and nobody had
seen it: no lane in this workspace runs this crate's tests on Windows
(`full_gate` is macOS/aarch64, CI is `ubuntu-latest`). That is the platform
axis one level in from where AGENTS.md applies it — not "a `--target` you never
pass is a platform you never compile", but *a platform you never EXECUTE on is
a set of assertions you have never read*.

⚠ The new arm is itself platform-dependent, written down as a limit rather
than a defect: it reds under perturbation on Windows and is VACUOUS on POSIX,
and the stronger-looking all-`\` fixture passes on Windows and reds on POSIX
for the opposite reason. **There is no separator fixture sound on both.** The
standing gap — nothing automatic runs this crate on Windows — is the owner's
call: a `windows-latest` job, or an explicit decision that Windows is
unsupported, which is the current *de facto* state without anyone having
chosen it.

Gates: `--lib` 1594 passed / 0 failed / 11 ignored at
`clippy_verify,rust_perf,rust_perf_bench,rust_perf_verify` (was 1585 / 8
failed); `--ignored` 11 passed (the real-cargo oracle tests, end to end);
clippy `--all-targets` 0 findings. Perturbation: 9 fixtures red with the
normalisation removed, 3 with the keyed names removed.

⛔ These oracle modules are feature-gated, so a plain `cargo test --lib`
compiles them to NOTHING — `-- prepare_crate` printed `running 0 tests` with a
green exit. Any gate row covering this code must name the features.

Landed at `9443ef1a`; the fleet-binary follow-up closed the same morning on the
M3: the global binary rebuilt from `3cfa4faf` with the release set (the fix was
4 commits ahead of the installed binary), and the AGENTS.md global-binary
bullet's `fix_verify,clippy_verify` wording corrected at `78c3c42f` — that set
could not build the cargo-heal bin at all (`required-features =
latent_retrieval,rust_perf,clippy_lints,kat_service`), so the symlink silently
keeps resolving to whatever binary was already there. Issue files removed per
the noise-reduction rule.

⛔ **Its one ⛔UNDETERMINED item was answered the same day, and the sentence
that recorded it was too strong** (Issue 112 Half A). It read *"nothing
recorded the environment, so this cannot be answered from the artifacts."*
Nothing recorded the ENVIRONMENT — but two of the three sites emit a quantity
a replay necessarily DESTROYS, and it is in the committed rows. The question
was never "what does the provenance field say"; it was "is there anything in
the output a replay could not have produced."

- `ClippyVerifier`: `control_fires` (the Bench 039 scaffold, built for an
  unrelated reason) is a per-CASE positive control, and a contaminated
  multi-case run drives it to ~1 — every `verify()` after the first replays
  the first's diagnostics, so from case 2 on it asks whether case 1's module
  trips case *k*'s lint. All **8** rows of `fixer_quality_history.jsonl` sit
  at `n` or `n − 1`, the shortfall reproducing at the same count across two
  different models, which is a per-SAMPLE property rather than a run one.
- `PerfBenchValidator`: a replay times ONE binary for every rule, so the
  numbers would coincide. Bench 013 — the GOAT that promoted `rust_perf` to
  default-on, and so the highest-stakes row in the repo — has **31 of 31**
  numeric speedup profiles distinct; the only repeated profile is the empty
  one shared by its 8 `NotBenchable` rows.
- `PerfVerifier`: no shipped artifact was ever produced by it. Its only
  appearance across `.benchmarks/`, `.docs/` and `.plans/` is Bench 019's G3
  row recording that the feature *type-checks*.

What stays open is riir-train's `data/` miss-shape corpus (its Issue 555) and
any uncommitted local `--verify` run, which left no artifact and is
unadjudicable by construction.

## 2026-09-16 — P30: the bench-target guard (rust_perf edits declined-and-flagged on measurement targets)

The 2026-09-16 intake (a katgpt-rs clippy-sweep session, `448c77f91`): a dry
run over `crates/katgpt-core/benches/bench_775_adjoint_goat.rs` proposed
`[perf] dead-result-timing-loop-folded-under-lto → std::hint::black_box` (+
loop/alloc restructures) at bench spans. Applying any of them changes WHAT the
bench measures — `--verify` compiles baseline/after but cannot know whether
the measured quantity survived; a benchmark file's numbers ARE its artifact
(GOAT gate evidence), and a timing loop folded under LTO is often precisely
the defect the bench exists to expose. The session declined manually and
filed the class in the cargo-heal skill's divergence table; the intake asked
for DECLINE-OR-FLAG automated at the lane — "a flag, not silence, so the
operator sees why the bench lint was left standing."

Landed as `src/domains/rust_perf/bench_guard.rs` + lane wiring in
`src/bin/heal.rs`. Detection (`is_bench_target(path, src)`) is deliberately
conservative — over-match is a loud, overridable false decline; under-match
is the silent defect: (a) path axis, any `benches` component (a bench target
AND every helper module under it — a perf edit in bench setup can alter the
measured section it feeds); (b) syntax axis, string-contains over the harness
signatures (`#[bench]`, `criterion_group!`/`criterion_main!`,
`bench_function(`, `#[divan::bench]`, `iai::bench`, `bencher::`) — a comment
mentioning a harness over-matches, documented. NOT a marker:
`std::hint::black_box` in source — it is the FIX half of perf rules and legal
in production code.

Policy scope — PERF domain only, both lanes: the fix lane collects perf
proposals into a side vec and declines them (pass-0 count, loud
`bench-guard:` stderr line per file + a run-summary line; the edits never
enter `edits`/verify batches, so `--verify`/write paths are covered by
construction), and `reheat_fix_pass` carries the same guard. The suggest lane
keeps every row visible but stamps perf rows on a bench target with
`⚠ bench-guard: applying perf rules here alters what the bench measures —
apply manually only`. Clippy lints, the rustc_errors `--fix-compile` lane
(making a bench COMPILE is not measurement-altering), sec, docker, dist are
out of scope by the recorded defect class.

Live-fire validation (built bin, `latent_retrieval,kat_service`): the
synthetic `benches/spec2.rs` specimen (static-str + vec-with-capacity shapes)
— `--fix` declined exactly the 4 perf edits with both lines and left the
file byte-identical, while the identical shapes in a plain `src/` file
applied the same 4 edits (`Vec::with_capacity(n)`, `const fn … &'static str`);
`--suggest` marked every perf row on the bench file (0 markers on the plain
file). Full-circle: the intake's exact specimen re-run with the guard —
`dead-result-timing-loop-folded-under-lto` at score 71.01 now carries the
`⚠ bench-guard` marker (30 perf-row markers total on that file; run under
`RIIR_HEAL_AUTO_ORACLE=0` — the Issue-113 auto-oracle spawns a whole-workspace
clippy for a katgpt-rs path, minutes by itself and orthogonal to this gate).

Gates: +10 bench_guard unit tests (path/syntax axes, the intake specimen
path, Windows separators, `benches_prefix` non-component negative,
black_box-not-a-marker, comment over-match documented) — lib 1560/1560
(default), 1710/1710 (latent_retrieval), clippy `-D warnings` clean at the
`latent_retrieval,kat_service,kat_transport,fix_verify` set; compiles at all
checked feature states. Score-bench + retrieval floors structurally
unaffected (no corpus/proposer/matcher change — lane policy only) and not
re-run.

Residue counted (the guard-landing protocol): workspace heal history mined

## 2026-09-16 — P33: use-row lexical scoping (platform-audit; the riir-chain `BrowserNodeState` intake)

The 09-16 quiet-repo batch's riir-chain platform-audit FP, fixed at the
classifier: a PRIVATE import inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`
(`crates/riir-chaind/src/browser/node.rs:138`, `use super::BrowserNodeState;`)
flagged `[PLATFORM-DEAD]` off `target_arch = "wasm32"` atoms attributed from
TWO type-path uses at file ROOT (`pub state: BrowserNodeState` / `pub fn
state(&self) -> BrowserNodeState`, both inside the wasm32-gated
`BrowserMeshNode`) — mentions that reference the ENUM, not the test-scoped
binding, pooled in by the name-global last-segment law. The pair was
internally inconsistent into the bargain: the enum decl itself stayed clean
precisely BECAUSE the ungated import counted as an ungated source reference —
under a scoping-correct model both cannot hold.

The fix (an import's binding is visible only inside its own module subtree):

- `UseSinks` bundles the evidence maps; a new per-(file → lexical scope →
  name) map records every mention's inline-mod scope (threaded through
  `walk_items`).
- A module-PRIVATE use row reads ONLY same-file mentions at its scope or
  DESCENDANT scopes (`T.starts_with(S)` — child scopes see parent bindings;
  ancestors, siblings, and other files cannot). An import with no in-scope
  mention is rustc's unused-import class, not a platform row (no_use).
- Non-private imports (`pub`/`pub(crate)`/… — the re-export surface) keep the
  name-global evidence: they are reachable from any module.

Measured (new binary vs the P31 global, side by side):

- **riir-chain: CLEAN** — the `BrowserNodeState` row is gone (was the repo's
  only row). No code change in riir-chain (gating the import wasm32-only
  E0432s the host test build; gating enum+tests orphans the tests — the
  cfg-green-zero trap; the classifier was the wrong half).
- **The two standing `use anyhow::Context` rows (riir-mmorpg-examples
  warm-tier-do host.rs + riir-deployer cloudflare DO host) are mechanized
  away** — both were adjudicated trait-method-consumption FPs whose only
  "evidence" was cross-file name-global phantom mentions (`.context()` is a
  method call, never path-visible); private-import scoping drops them. Both
  repos now measure CLEAN.
- **Full workspace platform re-sweep (every repo on disk): every repo CLEAN
  except self's standing `ECHO_DAEMON` (const — value-decl path, unchanged)**
  — the hardening direction (out-of-scope ungated mentions no longer
  suppress) surfaced ZERO new rows anywhere.
- riir-dapps stays clean (`ACCOUNT_HEADER` was fixed in-repo at `19abde1`).

+4 fixtures: the chaind specimen shape (out-of-scope uses don't flag the
test-scoped import), the hardening direction (in-scope gated uses flag
DESPITE an out-of-scope ungated mention that pre-fix suppressed the row —
evidence the cut restores true positives, not just kills FPs), pub-reexport
rows keep name-global evidence (the private twin flags), and cross-file
mentions are not evidence for a private import. Lib 1590/1590 in the shared
tree (includes concurrent sibling tests), clippy clean on the touched files.

## 2026-09-16 — P32: the `[C2·test-rig]` downgrade (config-audit; the riir-ai `Outcome`/`ProbeConfig` intake)

The 09-16 quiet-repo batch's other classifier intake: 2 of riir-ai's 3 [C2]
rows were test RIGS — `Outcome` (`riir-engine` `tests/cgsp_rewind_recovery_poc.rs:101`)
and `ProbeConfig` (`riir-gpu` `tests/support/gpu_exclusivity.rs:324`) — both
with LIVE in-rig field reads that read as confined test context only because
the entire file is a test. The C2 class was built for PRODUCTION config
structs whose consumer never materialized (the `PetAiConfig` canonical TP); a
struct that lives wholly in the tests tree is definitionally confined — it
cannot be production config (tests files do not compile into the lib).

## 2026-09-15 — Intake class P23: the `useless_format` escape guard on the oracle lane (clippy's own suggestion, refused where it is wrong)

The 09-14 intake row recorded a divergence class with a HALF-STALE premise:
it claimed "no `useless_format` fix-space" exists, but the Issue-016
expansion had shipped one long since — the PROPOSER refuses any brace in the
literal (its own v1 guard, `useless_format.rs:113`), which is exactly the
class the row wanted covered. What the row's claim WAS right about, without
naming it, is the door the fix actually needed: the P21 oracle lane consumes
clippy's own MachineApplicable suggestion children VERBATIM for every lint
in `FIXABLE_LINTS` — and `useless_format` is in that set. On an
escape-carrying literal, clippy's suggestion reuses the ESCAPED literal
text in a `.to_string()` position: `format!("{{x}}")` produces `{x}`, but
`"{{x}}".to_string()` produces `{{x}}` — the behavior change that corrupted
a JSON fixture from 1 parsed row to 0 in the original incident.

**The fix** (`src/draft/clippy_feed.rs`, `oracle_edits`): a `useless_format`
diagnostic whose covered call text contains ANY brace is dropped before the
candidate push. Sound by construction — any brace in a compiling no-args
`format!` literal is an escape (a lone brace would not compile), so
brace-present ⇔ the escape class; the drop is conservative in the only
direction that matters (a dropped edit, never a wrong one). It mirrors the
proposer's generation-time guard at the oracle door — the two paths now
agree on the shape. Documented divergence: the single-arg `{}`
`to_string()`-arg shape rides the same refusal when it reaches the oracle
lane (its `{}` placeholder trips the brace check); in practice the proposer
fires on that shape first and the bin's proposer-wins-on-overlap rule
handles it — the oracle lane only sees proposer-refused spans.

**Gates:** 2 new fixtures (`oracle_edits_refuse_useless_format_brace_escapes`
+ the brace-free control `oracle_edits_consume_useless_format_brace_free`);
clippy_feed 20/20; latent lib 1665 passed + 1 ignored; default lib 1515/1515
(unchanged — the module is `latent_retrieval`-gated); clippy
`-D warnings` clean at the touched surface; score-bench FLAT
(96.2% / 1.9% / 64 edits, row #116 — the guard is not on the bench path).

**Intake hygiene in the same commit:** the 6 stale opponent-watch rows
(09-07/08/10/12/13/13#2) flipped `[ ]`→`[x]` — completed records whose
open checkboxes were misrepresenting the live queue and costing re-triage
(the consuming session re-read all six this cycle); the 09-09 DISTILL
VERDICT row closed with a verified residue note (the `install.ps1`
asset-name half is FIXED at gist-rs/cargo-heal main HEAD — the probe accepts
both msvc and gnu asset names, verified by remote read; the `heal.gist.rs`
DNS half superseded by the v0.1.4 default-URL flip + fallback chain). The 4
open P14 rows stand (the (j)(k) tooling classes + the kernel mining leads —
real candidates, homes blocked or batch-gated).

## Issue 107 T2 — the span-shape embedding column lands (write-time capture) + the embed arm (`src/span_embed.rs`)

The revival-path column T1 named as the lane's only hope: every fixseq ring
row now carries a deterministic modelless embedding of the span's
ATTEMPT-TIME trigger text, and `--horizon-report` grew the arm that reads it.

- **Write-time capture, not offline re-embed** (the `latent-encode-at-capture`
  rule): the site's bytes DRIFT as fixes land — the ring exists to record a
  mutating loop — and `span_hash` is a SITE id (blake3 of `file:line`), not a
  content hash. Re-embedding offline would hash post-run bytes for a pre-fix
  state; the column lands at the one `push_attempt` chokepoint every attempt
  path funnels through (kept, no-progress, io, span-drift — all five sites).
- **The embedding** (`src/span_embed.rs`, ungated — blake3 is an
  unconditional dep): hashed unigram+bigram bag over tokenized trigger text
  (ident runs + single-char sigils, whitespace dropped), signed
  feature-hashing (bucket + sign from independent hash bytes — collisions
  cancel in expectation, not co-add), L2-normalized, ×127 i8-quantized.
  Integer-stamped so `AttemptRecord` keeps `Eq` (the Issue-105 u32 precedent);
  `#[serde(default)] Option<[i8; 32]>` so pre-T2 rings decode as `None`.
  7 module tests (determinism, whitespace-insensitivity, order sensitivity
  beyond unigrams, quantization-norm bound, non-ASCII folding).
- **The consumer** (horizon_report): `ridge_fit` went const-generic
  (`<const N: usize>` — the 9-native and 41-embed arms share it verbatim),
  `RingLine` mirrors the column, `auc(embed)` on pooled + family rows,
  `HORIZON(embed)` verdict line. **Full-coverage discipline**: the arm runs
  only when EVERY line of every run carries the column — a partial corpus
  skips LOUD with the coverage count in the header, never silently narrows
  the sample set beside native rows it would not be comparable with.
- **Two-sided canaries** (the T1 discipline held): the planted-content
  revival test — the label at i is the TOKEN CONTENT of line i-1
  (keep-marker vs revert-marker text) while every native scalar is constant
  and `kept_j` sees only the label sequence's mild lag-1 autocorrelation →
  `auc_embed ≥ 0.9` with native `< 0.9`; the identical-embeddings negative
  control (must not beat the floor); the coverage-skip test
  (`SKIPPED … 16/20` rendered). Design note from the fixture: KKRR-rotated
  label patterns (zero lag-1 autocorrelation, position-balanced when
  pooled) replace alternating ones — an alternating label pattern is
  perfectly learnable from `kept_j` (the alternation trap, T1's own lesson).
- **The measurement** (production path: `fixseq_prevalence --interacting
  --store` → real driver → real dump → real report): 46 cases, 116 attempts,
  `embed arm: ON (116/116)`. **The column does NOT revive the lane on
  synthetic corpora either: auc(embed) = 1.000 WITH history floor 1.000 at
  k=1 — BELOW-FLOOR**, the same sufficient-statistic verdict as T1 — the
  diverged arms share templates, so span content carries no signal the
  strategy prior lacks. The revival question now rests on ORGANIC rings,
  which start accumulating the column at write time from this landing
  (every future `--fix-compile --write` run).
- **Drive-by repair surfaced by the new field**: `tests/nonergodic_driver_ab.rs`'s
  `AttemptRecord` literal predated the Issue-105 journey fields — a latent
  compile break behind the opt-in `nonergodic_driver` feature (the
  cfg-gated-target trap), fixed with the fields + a naming comment.
- Validation: lib 1462/1462 (9 new), `fix_compile` e2e green with
  embed-equality assertions on both kept + revert paths (the embedding is a
  pure function of the attempt-time trigger text — byte-reproducible),
  `journey_credit_gate` 3/3, `nonergodic_driver` compile-checked, clippy
  clean (lib, bin, tests, examples — plus the healer's 3 mechanical edits
  and one manual `is_multiple_of` fix in a pre-existing T1 test line).

## Issue 107 T1 — the fixseq horizon report + the lane-viability verdict (`src/horizon_report.rs`)

Issue 107's first task: is an attempt's outcome linearly decodable from the
ring state k attempts earlier, at an AUC that beats both floors? The
instrument + the honest first measurement, plus the cross-repo repair it
unblocked.

- **riir-kat `4bc8672` (the unblock)**: the previous session's `a80ec7a`
  left the replay client's transport-tier imports ungated — `HttpResponse`
  and the tests' `MockTransport` resolved `kat_transport`-gated items
  unconditionally, so a default-features `cargo check` in riir-kat (and
  riir-clippy's `kat_service` lane) failed E0432. The session that shipped
  it had validated only under kat_transport builds — the count-identical
  trap in feature form. Fixed by mirroring `kat_burn_client`'s own
  cfg'd-import precedent (4 attribute lines).
- **The instrument** (`src/horizon_report.rs`, ungated pure stats — the
  `frontier_report` store-free law): a local `RingLine` wire mirror of the
  ring jsonl (same `#[serde(default)]` legacy compat as `AttemptRecord`),
  strict-lead features at i-k (nothing from `(i-k, i]`), LORO-held-out
  closed-form ridge readout, base floor 0.5 + per-strategy Laplace-prior
  floor (same fold — no leakage), per-target-code family rows at k=1, and
  the three refusal classes (EMPTY / BLIND WALK / SINGLE CLASS — never a
  green zero). 8 module tests incl. the two-sided canary: a planted lead-2
  signal decodes at AUC ≥ 0.9 while exact-tie constant features yield
  exactly 0.5 / horizon-none (the alternation trap is documented in the
  test — any alternating label pattern is perfectly learnable from `kept_j`
  and IS signal, so the no-signal fixture ties scores by construction).
- **The measurement** (rings regenerated via `fixseq_prevalence --store`,
  the production CompileDriver — synthetic corpora, the standing label;
  ZERO organic rings exist workspace-wide): single (126 runs) → BLIND WALK
  (all 1-attempt — matches Bench 088's 1.00-decisions/run); multi5 (24) →
  SINGLE CLASS (base rate 1.000, the Bench 045 first-try-perfect class);
  interacting (46) → readout AUC 1.000 WITH history floor 1.000 at k=1 —
  BELOW-FLOOR, the sufficient-statistic verdict: on this corpus outcomes
  are strategy-determined, so no feature set can beat the prior; pooled
  (196) → HORIZON = 1 (< 2), all k≥2 rows single-class.
- **The verdict**: `horizon ≥ 2 does NOT pay` on ring-native features —
  T2's embedding column is the probe lane's only revival path, and the
  organic surface stays the real open question. The k=1 pooled OK is a
  pooling artifact (cross-corpus strategy-prior contamination) —
  per-corpus reads are primary, footnoted in the issue.

## P21 post-mining intake — the oracle-suggestion-children consumption: the `--clippy-json` fix lane applies clippy's own MachineApplicable suggestions verbatim (the P15 Unknown-receiver residue closed) (2026-09-14)

The P13 row's named open followup ("the knowable route is oracle-fed"),
executed the day after P15 left it as residue. The shape: our
`unnecessary_map_or` proposer refuses type-UNKNOWN receivers standalone
(E0599-unsafe — `is_some_and` on a `Result` is a compile error), but real
clippy's suggestion at those spans is TYPE-AWARE and exact. In
`--clippy-json` mode the diagnostic's own suggestion children now close
that gap IN the healer's pipeline (verify gate, trajectory rows,
provenance) instead of leaking to `cargo clippy --fix` one-offs.

**Probe-first (`.raw/oracle_probe`, clippy 1.98 — deleted after):** the
intake's "consume the suggestion verbatim" premise was HALF-wrong — the
suggestion for `unnecessary_map_or` is NOT a single whole-call replacement.
It is a TWO-PART suggestion inside ONE child: `map_or` → `is_some_and`
(bytes 467–473) plus a DELETION of `false, ` (474–481, replacement `""`),
with the `(` gap byte PRESERVED between them. Three facts that shaped the
implementation: (1) an empty `""` replacement is a real part (a deletion)
— only JSON `null` means "not an edit part"; (2) gap bytes between parts
are kept unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION in rustc multipart suggestions, so a
merge that copies gap text verbatim is semantics-preserving for every
well-formed suggestion; (3) child-0 ("for further information") carries
no spans — only children with replacement spans count.

**The landing (3 pieces):**

1. **`FeedSuggestion` capture** (`src/draft/clippy_feed.rs`) — the first
   help child's replacement parts, sorted, when EVERY part is
   `MachineApplicable`, in the primary file, byte-ordered. All-or-nothing
   refusals: `MaybeIncorrect` grades, multi-CHILD suggestions (the
   move/insert class — applying half a move is a corrupted file),
   cross-file parts, overlapping parts. Feed dedup upgraded to
   key-on-`(file, line, lint)` with a suggestion UPGRADE path (a repeat
   occurrence upgrades a suggestion-less first row).
2. **`oracle_edits` — the merge + the gates.** Parts merge into ONE
   atomic edit (replacement = parts joined with the ORIGINAL gap text
   preserved verbatim; `map_or(false, ` → `is_some_and(` byte-exact), so
   the emitter can never partially apply a suggestion. Guards, in order:
   lint must be in the fix lane's `lint_set` (the corpus-rule
   precondition — the healer never becomes a generic `cargo clippy
   --fix` re-run; gap lints stay the suggest lane's `[no corpus rule]`
   signal); stale-offset/boundary refusal; oracle-vs-oracle overlap
   (leftmost wins); and a WHOLE-FILE PARSE GATE — the oracle edits alone,
   spliced into a copy, must leave the file parseable, all-or-nothing.
   That gate caught its own author mid-landing: the first draft of the
   zero-width-insertion test fixture inserted `#[inline] ` mid-expression
   and the gate refused it — the fixture was wrong, not the code.
3. **The bin wiring** (`src/bin/heal.rs`, pass 0 of the fixpoint loop) —
   oracle edits join the pass-0 edit set after the proposer collection,
   PROPOSER EDITS WIN on overlap (an oracle edit inside a proposer's
   rewrite is stale by construction), review lines carry the
   `oracle-anchored:` note, the run summary prints `N oracle edits
   applied`, and drops surface LOUDLY (`oracle lane: dropped N
   suggestion(s) … does the feed match the current tree state?`).
   `lint_set` iteration moved to `for &lint in &lint_set` (borrow, not
   move — the merge needs the set after the loop).

**Live e2e (the probe crate, the real binary, `--fix --verify`):** three
Unknown receivers — `items.iter().min().map_or(false, ..)` (`.min()` is
an unlisted Option shape), `File::open(p).map_or(false, ..)` (Result via
an unlisted bare call), `x.as_ref().map_or(false, ..)` (the documented
kind-preserving divergence) — all three applied verbatim
(`is_some_and`/`is_ok_and`/`is_some_and` — clippy's type-aware choice at
each, which the parse-only proposer could never make), compile-gated (2
cargo checks, 0 reverts), post-heal real clippy reports 0 findings. The
STALE-FEED re-run (same feed against the healed file, offsets shifted):
loud drop of all 3 + the file byte-IDENTICAL — the parse gate refused
the misaligned splice, zero corruption. **The e2e also exposed a live
asymmetry worth knowing:** the suggest lane's `[oracle] unnecessary_map_or
NO CORPUS RULE` comes from the LEASED corpus (its epoch predates P15's
corpus row) while the fix lane consumes from the compiled-in
`FIXABLE_LINTS` — the suggest lane's rule book is retrieval truth, the
fix lane's lint_set is fix truth, and for freshly-landed lints they can
disagree until the lease refreshes.

**Gates:** clippy_feed 18/18 (13 new); default lib 1441/1441 (unchanged —
`draft` is latent-gated), latent 1589/1589, all-features 2332/2332,
clippy clean; score-bench FLAT. Docs: `unnecessary_map_or.rs` divergence
bullet flipped to CLOSED, `--clippy-json` help + AGENTS bullet extended,

## P15 post-mining intake — `unnecessary_map_or` lands: the born-lint closure, the `receiver_kind` substrate extraction + the SAFE-LET extension, and the gen2/gen3 re-freeze (2026-09-14)

The P13 row's named candidate followup, executed same-day: the healer's own
`map_unwrap_or` fallback emits `map_or(false, f)` at type-UNKNOWN receivers
(the always-compiling choice), and real clippy immediately re-flags that
output as `unnecessary_map_or` — the gen-8 shaped-verdict family's fourth
measured member. This unit closes the loop.

**Probe-first (`.raw/mapor_probe`, clippy 1.98, deleted after):** the full
firing envelope — Option+`false`→`is_some_and`, Option+`true`→`is_none_or`
(`map_or(true,f) ≡ is_none_or(f)` EXACTLY — no negation requirement, the
plain shape fires), Result+`false`→`is_ok_and`, all MachineApplicable
method-name suggestions; Result+`true` clippy-SILENT (no `is_err_or` in std
— `map_or(true,f)` IS terminal there); `map_or_else(|| false, f)` SILENT
under both `unnecessary_map_or` and `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` (out of
clippy's envelope — mirrored). Local-binding receivers (the born-lint
class) FIRE in real clippy — the gap was ours, not clippy's.

**The landing (3 pieces):**

1. **The `receiver_kind` substrate extraction** — `ReceiverKind` +
   `classify_receiver` + param/fn-ret classification moved from
   `map_unwrap_or.rs` to the shared `proposers/receiver_kind.rs` (the
   DRY-minimal home now that two rules need it). En route fix: `fn_rets` is
   now a file-wide PRE-PASS (forward calls to later-defined fns classify;
   the v1 during-visit collection missed every forward reference).
2. **The SAFE-LET extension** (the substrate's addition, closes the
   cascade at its SOURCE): `let best = v.iter().find(..); best.map_or(..)`
   classifies `best` OptionLike. SOUND by construction — a binding
   qualifies only when the name is bound EXACTLY ONCE in the whole fn (no
   shadowing let/match/for/closure binding anywhere), never assigned
   (plain + all 10 compound-assign forms), and not a param name: a Rust
   binding has one static type, so every bare use refers to the one
   binding whose type is its initializer's. Benefits BOTH rules
   (`map_unwrap_or` now emits the terminal form directly at safe-let
   sites instead of birthing the lint).
3. **The `unnecessary_map_or` proposer** — fires ONLY on receivers PROVEN
   Option/Result (params, safe-lets, shape allowlists, same-file fn rets);
   Unknown REFUSES (the documented divergence — `is_some_and` on a Result
   is a hard E0599, the bench_440 class; the `--clippy-json` oracle lane is
   the designed close for the residue). `.as_ref()` chains are a measured
   divergence: kind-preserving on BOTH Option and Result, unclassifiable
   from text (pinned by test). FIXABLE tier (39th row). 17 unit tests +
   11 substrate tests.

**The gen2/gen3 re-freeze (the loudness gate working as designed):**
adding the atom grew the ladder 38→39 and reshuffled every stride window
past it — the `freeze_status_holes_are_loud` gates caught the new unlabeled
specs exactly as built. Both tables regenerated deterministically (labels
= per-atom expects; windows containing the two bad atoms excluded — the
one NEW exclusion is the reshuffled
`gen2-k3-uninlined_format_args+unnecessary_lazy_evaluations+unnecessary_map_or`),
then **re-verified against real clippy** (v2 e2e 30.6 s: 67 verified / 0
newly excluded / 0 drift; v3 e2e 23.6 s: 73 verified / 0 newly excluded —
the new atom fires exactly its own lint, zero new interference). Corpus
53→54 (count pins updated); FIXABLE 38→39.

unfamiliar `after` sha read as "older" without ever running `git log` on
it, and every subsequent observation felt like confirmation. The
one-command test that settles any "history loss" allegation:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/<branch> && echo INTACT`.

## P12 post-mining intake — `needless_pass_by_ref_mut` lands: the 2026-09-09 nursery-gap row closes, probe-corrected twice (2026-09-14)

The last open clippy_lints intake candidate (the ~80-finding riir-ai sweep
row). Corpus 52 → 53, VERIFY-tier 11 → 12 (38 `--fix` / 12 `--verify` /
3 self_evolve-only).

**The probe (`.raw/pbrm_probe`, clippy 0.1.98 / 48a229ceae, deleted after
the landing) corrected the intake row TWICE before anything landed** (the
P10/P11/P12 pattern, 4th consecutive):

1. **The real firing surface is narrower than the row implied**: `pub`
   methods are SILENT (clippy's exported-API guard — the round-1 probe fired
   only the ONE private method among five read-only candidates), `pub(crate)`
   FIRES, trait-impl methods are SILENT (an impl cannot relax its trait's
   receiver), and private FREE fns with `&mut` params fire too (out of scope
   v1 — receiver-only, the documented divergence). The proposer mirrors the
   visibility line exactly (private + `pub(crate)` only, inherent impls
   only).
2. **The "must emit BOTH halves or the fix does not verify" premise was
   factually wrong at the gate level**: the fix_verify gate is errors-only
   ("Warnings do not fail the check", `fix_verify.rs` header) — a
   definition-site fix VERIFIES fine (the caller-side `unused_mut` cascade
   is a warning). AND real clippy's own suggestion is definition-site-ONLY
   (applicability `Unspecified` — `cargo clippy --fix` applied 0 edits,
   probed): the cascade was never part of the lint's fix; it is rustc's
   separate machine-applicable `unused_mut` pass. The cascade still matters
   for `-D warnings` consumer CIs (a left-over `unused_mut` is a new
   warning attributable to our edit), so the proposer emits it anyway — but
   as a NARROW provable shape, not a gate requirement.

**The proposer** (`src/domains/clippy_lints/proposers/needless_pass_by_ref_mut.rs`):

- **Definition half**: `&mut self` → `&self` (node-span replacement,
  byte-clean) on eligible methods — non-`pub` inherent-impl methods, plain
  `&mut self` receiver (syn 2 carries the mut in `Receiver::mutability`,
  NOT the reference tuple — the first-implementation bug the unit tests
  caught), plain fn (no attrs/async/const/unsafe/abi/variadic).
- **Body analysis** (parse-only approximation of clippy's type-aware
  "never uses `self` mutably"): refuse on assignment/compound-assign LHS
  rooted at `self`, `&mut` operands mentioning `self` anywhere, macros
  whose tokens mention `self` (`write!(self.buf, ..)` — macro bodies are
  invisible), bare-`self` paths outside allowed positions, and self-rooted
  method calls UNLESS the callee is on the std-`&self` allowlist (16
  entries — the `needless_borrow` receiver-whitelist precedent) or resolves
  to exactly ONE same-file `&self` declaration (a `&mut` callee this pass
  fixes becomes visible to callers NEXT fixpoint pass — the 4-pass
  composition, not intra-pass cleverness). A custom type overriding
  `len(&mut self)` is the documented divergence — E0596, revertable by the
  compile gate (the tier argument: every wrong fire on BOTH halves is a
  check-visible compile error).
- **Cascade half**: drop `mut` from `let mut x` when EVERY mention of the
  binding inside its enclosing fn (locals are fn-scoped — the fn range is
  the complete use set) is the receiver of a call to a method this pass
  fixed, the method name is declared exactly once in the file (no
  cross-type ambiguity), and no same-name re-let shadows it. Any other use
  shape — assignment, `&mut`, field write, an unfixed method call, a
  by-value pass, a macro — leaves the `mut` alone (the left-over is
  rustc's machine-applicable `unused_mut`, never a break).

**Tier**: VERIFY (`VERIFY_LINTS`) — the lint is nursery/default-`allow` (a
default-flags verify compiles the rule to a no-op — the lint-flavored
cfg-gate lesson), consumed via the `--clippy-json` oracle lane. Live-fired
end-to-end through the real binary: `-W clippy::needless-pass-by-ref-mut`
JSON feed → `--suggest --clippy-json` surfaces `[oracle] needless_pass_by_ref_mut
oracle finding` at the real span, footer `0 no-corpus-rule`, fixture
top-ranked at 319.46. (Operational note en route: the run initially printed
`NO CORPUS RULE` — the kat corpus LEASE (epoch 2958, `.heal/corpus-lease`)
REPLACES the compiled-in corpus at runtime, and the leased epoch predates
the entry; the gap signal was honest for that config. Bypassing the lease
showed the compiled-in truth. The rule reaches leased users at the next
service-side corpus sync.)

**Real-clippy fixture validation** (the P10/P11 discipline): buggy fires
under `-W` at exactly the `read` method; fixed is clean; DEFAULT-level
output carries ZERO real diagnostics (the cascade half verified — no
left-over `unused_mut`).

**Gates**: 19 proposer unit tests (fire/silent per probe shape: pub silent,
`pub(crate)` fires, trait impl silent, transitive-`&mut`-callee silent,
shared-callee fires, allowlisted chain fires, ambiguous callee silent,
macro/self-arg/async silent; cascade fire + 3 refusals) + corpus
`corpus_size_is_53` + `all_buggy_codes_fire_their_lint` + fixture-table row
+ `fixable_lints_exclude_type_blind_rules` row. lib 1404/1404 (was 1385),
latent 1539/1539, all-features 2282/2282, clippy `-D warnings --all-targets`
clean. Score-bench FLAT at the pinned 96.2/1.9/100/100 (64 edits) — the
frozen v1 fixture set is unperturbed.

**Rider**: `src/downstream_hint.rs` — the previous session's committed
test code carried two clippy findings invisible to a `--lib`-only clippy
run (an unused `b` binding at L329; a `&format!(..)` needless borrow at
L352 — both test-only, both fixed here; the session's "clippy clean" claim
was made with `cargo clippy --lib` which does not lint `cfg(test)` code —

## P14 post-mining intake — the cross-repo consumer-surface hint landed: the FP-class #3 open candidate closes (2026-09-14)

The FP-class #3 row's last open candidate (family (b) probed dormant
2026-09-14; the cross-repo half was "the bigger measured share and has NO
instrument surface yet"). The 943 scoped-scan class measured 44% FP on a
NON-LEAF scan, and 4-of-7 FPs were **cross-repo production reads** — fields
DEFINED in the scanned repo, READ in a downstream sibling that imports its
crates (`SftWarmupConfig` dying at riir-train-gpu `pipeline.rs` while living
in riir-ai). Neither a wider intra-repo scope nor the existing scope hint
can see that blind half: the 943 pass was FULL-scope.

**Instrument: `src/downstream_hint.rs`** — after `--config-audit` /
`--orphan-report`, a one-line cross-repo hint naming every sibling repo ON
DISK whose manifests path-dep into the scanned repo, with the count of
DISTINCT dep-target crates (deduped across member manifests; dev-deps count
— the FP class includes test readers). Never widens the scan (the
scope_hint law); fires whenever ≥1 consumer exists, INCLUDING full `.`
scans (the difference from scope_hint's partial-widening gate — this blind
spot is not operator-made).

**Design decisions, both probe-forced:**

1. **Measured-graph discovery, NOT the BOUNDARY.md tables the intake
   row originally proposed.** `path = "..."` values in the sibling's
   manifests, canonicalized and prefix-matched against the scanned repo
   root (identifier-guarded textual scanner — no toml dep, the dist-domain
   hand-written-scanner precedent). Prose drifts (boundary-guard exists for
   that); manifests cannot. On-disk only — a partial-clone box names its
   subset, and "on disk" is in the message for that reason.
2. **Root + workspace-member manifests, NEVER a recursive tree walk.**
   The first shell probe (`find` over all sibling trees for Cargo.toml)
   TIMED OUT at 120s on this 24-dir Windows box (`zed`, `vendor`…).
   Discovery reads the sibling root Cargo.toml + declared `members` globs
   (multi-line array parsing included) + conventional `crates/*` /
   `examples/*` / `benches/*` probes — direct file opens, ~50 ms for the
   whole box.

The scanned repo root is the TOPMOST Cargo.toml-holding ancestor of the
first target (the workspace, not the nearest crate — a scan of `crates/x`
must name consumers of ANY crate in the repo, since reads of `crates/x`'s
types can sit in a sibling that deps a different crate). Repos only (a
`.git` FILE counts — linked worktrees are real read surfaces).

**Two test-fixture lessons worth keeping:** (1) the member-manifest
dep-path level count — from `repoB/crates/b`, `../../repoA` resolves to
`repoB/repoA` (two levels up is repoB, not the parent); members need
`../../../repoA`. Four fixtures had it wrong and the code was right — the
debug probe (canonicalize returning `Err(NotFound)` on `repoB\repoA`)
settled attribution in one run. (2) the topmost walk OVERSHOOTS a fake repo
nested inside a real repo tree (a fake under `target/` claims the REAL
repo as root) — correct behavior for the nested-repo shape, so the
relative-path test places its fake directly under the workspace root
(cwd's parent — same volume, no Cargo.toml above the fake).

**Validation:** 15 module tests (consumer naming, leaf silence, third-repo
and internal deps excluded, declared-member + conventional-member
discovery, dev-dep counting, dedupe, topmost walk, worktree `.git` file,
relative target, live-shape `src` leaf silence, scanner shapes, multi-line
members); lib 1385/1385; clippy clean on the module. Live probes through
the real binary: `--config-audit ../katgpt-rs` → **12 sibling repos**
(riir-ai 20 crates, riir-train 12, riir-auth 9, riir-dapps 9, riir-kat 9,
riir-chain 3, +6 more) — matching the independent shell-probe ground
truth exactly; `--config-audit .` on the leaf → silent; `--config-audit
src` (relative, from the scanned repo's CWD) → both hints fire;
`--config-audit ../riir-ai` → names **riir-train (10 crates) first** — the
exact 943 specimen consumer; `--orphan-report` on a fake → the hint prints
even on the blind-history-leg refusal path.

## `cargo heal --version` exit-2 regression — found by the global-binary rebuild, closed by merging the two hand-mirrored flag lists (2026-09-13, `ad31a04a`)

Rebuilding the global `cargo-heal` from HEAD (the staleness caveat — the
shipped binary was a Sep-10 build predating `--clippy-json`) surfaced a
live CLI regression: the fresh binary refused `--version` / `-V` with
"no paths given" + usage, exit 2, while the stale Sep-10 build printed
the version. Mechanism (git archaeology): the 2026-09-12 --misses fix
(`2cf731c0`) completed `is_bare_posture` with `!args.version` but the
paths guard — a SECOND hand-mirrored list inside `parse_args` — kept
its missing row; pre-09-12 `--version` had worked only because the bare
default accidentally armed `suggest` + `paths=["."]` under it, which
that fix correctly removed. Broken window: 2026-09-12 → 2026-09-13
(the documented contract — "--version prints and exits, any build,
ungated" — was right all along; the code was wrong).

Root-cause repair, not a row-add: both lists now consume ONE shared
`standalone_mode()` predicate (bare posture = no primary mode ∧ no
standalone mode; paths guard = the same predicate), so the mirror-drift
class the `standalone_modes_are_never_bare` pin warned about is
structurally closed — a future standalone mode adds ONE row in ONE
place. The pin test asserts BOTH consumers per mode. The global binary
was rebuilt from clean HEAD with the release feature set
(`default,latent_retrieval,kat_service,kat_transport,fix_verify`,
in-tree + isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` — a /tmp worktree breaks the
`../riir-ai/vendor` patch paths, measured) and copied over both
`target/release/cargo-heal.exe` and `~/.cargo/bin/cargo-heal.exe`;
`--version` verified exit 0 e2e.

## Issue 089 T4 hardening — the bench-tail frontier snapshot: generation boundaries record themselves (2026-09-13, `11c1799d`; the 7 lane runs + snapshot row #2 recorded the pre-rebase build sha `b17c2dd8` — identical diff, the rebase only moved the base)

The T4 evidence clock had a fragile half: a band-mass snapshot existed only
when somebody ran `--frontier-report` AT a generation boundary — but
boundaries are created by score-bench runs, and lanes interleave (v1 reruns
after v8 landings). A boundary nobody reports at is a boundary the
band-mass ↔ next-generation-yield correlation never samples. The fix is
mechanical: `finish_score_bench` (the ONE tail every generation lane runs —
clippy 1/2/3/6/7/8, compile 4, perf 5) now calls
`frontier_report::append_snapshot_at_frontier` right after its history
append + store dual-write, so the just-recorded run IS in `score_runs` and
a newly admitted generation raises the frontier in the same breath.

- Same committed file (`.benchmarks/frontier_snapshots.jsonl`), same
  state-change dedup, same FRONTIER-generation semantics as the report
  path — two writers, one law, no drift.
- `NoStore` / `EmptyPopulation` are SKIPS, never fabricated green-zero rows
  (the report law); best-effort — one console line, never a bench failure.
  A bench build without `latent_retrieval` prints the loud skip.
- 3 lib tests (latent_retrieval-gated): the skip laws + the
  append→dedup→generation-raise sequence (verdict seeding split from run
  seeding so the gen-9 boundary lands with an IDENTICAL band — the exact
  boundary-capture case).
- **Live validation, same session (7 lane runs at `b17c2dd8`):** the v1
  lane appended snapshot row #2 (gen-8, sha `b17c2dd8`, band-mass 5.6% —
  identical to row #1's metrics: the sha axis moved, the band did not);
  the six further lane runs each printed `unchanged — not appended`.
  Rows ≥ generations, exactly as designed.
- **T8 accumulation rode along** (rows #99-105): 8 rows now carry
  `rule_outcomes` across 7 generations (1/3/4/5/6/7/8). The gen-3 lane is
  the attribution-densest (36 rules); gen-4/5 carry the field with EMPTY
  attribution (composite fixtures — the skip is loud); gen-2 contributed
  NO row — the admission gate REFUSED its first append (heal_rate 1.0 ≥
  v1's 0.9623: the healer outgrew the v2 k-ladder; honest refusal, by
  design). The α grid-fit still waits on future generations.

Issue 089 remains OPEN on accumulation only: T4's ≥3 FUTURE generation
boundaries now self-record the moment generations 9+ land; T8's replay
corpus grows by one row per bench run. The gate stays unwired until the
evidence exists (report-first law).

## Issue 097 — linking↔confusion PoC: NO-GO, the fusion idea retired as measured-refuted; RESOLVED (2026-09-12)

The katgpt-rs Issue 757 follow-up gate ("no plan until a PoC on the
oracle-labeled fixtures exists") ran as `examples/linking_confusion_poc.rs`
behind `linking_confusion_poc` (the `gw_corpus` defend-wrong pattern):
93 rule clouds over the 101-span fixture canon (M=32 salted rename variants,
n=33/cloud, 8-D ModellessEmbedder), 2,158 within-domain pairs, 3,333
retrieval queries at 86.3% top-1 self rate (the confusion ground truth:
9 pairs pooled, 4 base-canon).

**Both config classes refute.** At the paper's config (k=8) the instrument
degenerates: k/n ≈ 0.24 vs the paper's ≤ 0.004 regime, 99.9–100% linked, |link|
up to 51 — zero binary discrimination. At the sensitivity control (k=3, k/n ≈
0.09) linking gains a 55.6% base rate and shows ANTI-enrichment (confusion mass
×0.48 pooled on linked vs unlinked; Fisher p=1.0 both arms). **The Spearman
trap is named in the record**: ρ reads 0.90/0.60 across the arms — invalid
under 99.6% ties at zero confusion, and it moved with the tie structure while
the confused-pair set stayed fixed. Do not re-derive it as a positive.

Mechanism: the paper's premise is smooth multi-exemplar class manifolds; the
fixtures give 1 exemplar/rule — rename ORBITS, combinatorially thin and
entangled under PCA-3D at any sane k. The manifold assumption fails on this
corpus exactly as the katgpt-rs Issue 757 follow-up feared. A corpus-scale boundary,
not a detector defect (katgpt-rs Bench 717 holds at its designed regime). Reopen
trigger: a real-repo mined span set (≥ hundreds of REAL spans/rule). The
`linking_fold_detector` stays opt-in with no consumer; the katgpt-rs Research 391
deferred guides stay deferred — their unblocker needs a different consumer
class. Reproduce: `cargo run --release --features linking_confusion_poc
--example linking_confusion_poc`.

## Orphan-report serde boundary — the riir-ai Issue 934 follow-on repair (2026-09-12, `d2e39d1f`)

The first consumer-repo landing produced the instrument's first measured
false-positive class, and the repair landed the same day. riir-ai Issue 934
(`08322e814`, the Plan-126 residue adjudication) found
`ConversationEntry.deadline_tick`/`.failed_at_tick` flagged stillborn while
being LIVE YAML-output schema: `add_auto_fail` populates both and the
`g4_2`/`g5_2b` tests pin their serialized presence. The derive reads fields
invisibly to the syntactic member-read tally — the known Serialize-only
exclusion, now in a Ser+De struct.

**The boundary is the ATTR, not the derive pair.** The probe evidence was
the riir-ai Issue 934 full flagged sample: `BehaviorConfig` itself derives BOTH
(round-trips YAML) and carried every true positive (`alarm_radius`,
`boids`, `initial_goal`) with plain `#[serde(default)]` attrs — a
Ser+De-pair exclusion would have killed the instrument's canonical case —
while the only two `skip_serializing_if` fields in the flagged set were
exactly the two false positives. Semantics: `skip_serializing_if` marks
conditionally-emitted OUTPUT-schema surface (the derive reads the field
when the condition holds); plain serde-default fields are persistence
mirrors whose functional read is what the report measures.
`#[serde(skip)]` stays a candidate — the derive never touches it, so a
never-member-read skip field is genuinely dead.

Implementation: `SerdeStructMarker` now also collects the per-struct
`skip_serializing_if` field set; `zero_external_read_fields` retains it
out of BOTH candidate paths (Default-impl and literal). Fixtures: the
exact `ConversationEntry` shape (regression pin) + the exact
`BehaviorConfig` Ser+De plain-default shape (the FN guard) — 39/39.
1247/0 lib; clippy `-D warnings` clean on both touched files (the 12
residual `--all-targets` findings are the known sibling
frontier/rustc_errors lane). AGENTS.md bullet + the `.distill` intake row
updated in-commit (`d585aae1`).

## Plan 126 — orphan-report: intake class C1, the config knob orphaned by optimization (2026-09-12)

The LAST open post-mining intake class, closing the 888-derived class-C
family (A/B Plan 124, C2 Plan 125). `cargo heal --orphan-report [PATHS…]`:
the review/sweep-time instrument the intake mandated — a two-leg REPORT
(current-state zero-external-read fields via the shared `config_audit`
scan core + git-history evidence of vanished read-shaped occurrences),
never a per-compile lint. Ungated, zero new deps (syn + git subprocess),
report-first; refuses exit 1 on an empty scan or a blind history leg (the
frontier-report law — never a confident green zero).

**Two findings that reshaped the instrument (both measured, both recorded
in the intake row):**

1. **The canonical case forced a serde-literal candidate extension.**
   `BehaviorConfig` has no `impl Default` — the designer surface is
   `#[serde(default)]` + handwritten literal tables (`hardcoded_config()`),
   so the A/B/C2 candidate net could not see the intake's OWN canonical
   case (`alarm_radius`). The orphan leg additionally collects
   constructor-init candidates from serde-backed structs (any `#[serde(…)]`
   on the item, or a derive naming Deserialize; Serialize-only excluded —
   the derive reads those fields invisibly and every one would read as a
   stillborn FP). Classes A/B/C2 deliberately keep the narrower net —
   their plans' measured rates stand.
2. **The intake's "reader that vanished" narrative is syntactically false
   for the canonical case.** Repo-wide pickaxe over ALL riir-ai history:
   `.alarm_radius` member-read occurrences never changed before the fix —
   the const-table fn was born 2026-06-06 (Plan 225 T2) and the config
   field 2026-06-08 (riir-ai Plan 245), two days LATER, with the values already
   copied into the table. The knob was BORN unwired, not orphaned by a
   refactor. The instrument fires it honestly as `[stillborn]` — first
   row at the pre-fix control tree (worktree of `88c51824b^`, sampled 9/9
   rows TRUE repo-wide). The ORPHANED machinery stays for real vanished
   readers: current riir-ai (2613 files) yields exactly one —
   `ReplayVerificationResponse.server_hash` (6→1 read-shaped occurrences
   across `23389c801` "refactor(570): dissolve riir-ffi"; the survivor is
   a test assert) — VERIFIED TRUE.

**Validation:** self-scan 1 TP / 0 FP (`PavDataConfig.ground_truth`); the
pre-fix control fires the canonical case; current-riir-ai stillborn sample
8 TRUE unwired knobs (civ `boids`/`initial_goal`/
`use_predator_weights` — the post-`alarm_radius` remainder of the same
designer surface; engine `default_tau_reliable`, `summary_kind`; rest
`server_hash`) + 3 benign-true (repr(C) Pod padding — the documented
benign subclass) / 0 FP. 37/37 fixtures (incl. a REAL-git e2e:
init→wire→optimize→orphan in a throwaway tempdir repo). 1241 lib green;
clippy clean on every touched file (healed first; the repo-wide `-D
warnings` residue is PRE-EXISTING in the 093/frontier lane's committed
files). Those stillborn rows are findings for their OWNING lanes —
recorded, not deleted (the instrument never edits).

**En-route lessons:** (a) `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns the
PHYSICAL path on macOS — canonicalize scan paths before `strip_prefix` or
every pathspec is silently dropped (the first e2e run read as BLIND);
(b) scanning the repo root itself yields an EMPTY rel — map it to the
whole-tree pathspec `.`, not to a dropped probe; (c) the probe-lattice +
pickaxe pair needs BOTH directions: the lattice proves the delta, the
pickaxe names the commit — neither alone convicts.

## Plan 125 — config-audit class C2: the self-referential config struct detector (2026-09-12)

The post-mining intake's top open class, consumed at the idle window (the
mining queue itself had NOTHING staged — B143 consumed the last PERF-SEARCH
row; this was the queue's correct next unit). Extends the Plan-124
`--config-audit` instrument with the C2 sub-shape: a whole struct whose
every Default-impl field has zero EXTERNAL reads — reads confined to its
own validate-shaped (`bool`/`Result`-returning) methods and test context.
Classes A/B require zero reads, so the internally-read orphan (the
PlasmaConfig shape) was invisible to them.

**The landing's own bug, caught by the probe:** syn 2 impl methods are
`syn::ImplItem::Fn` — the `visit_item_fn` visitor hook NEVER fires inside
impl blocks, so the validate-shape context (and with it the whole own-impl
tally) was silently empty and the C2-positive fixture read as live. The
temporary tally-probe printed `field_reads_in_impl: {}` over a fixture with
a validate() method — the fix is `visit_impl_item_fn` (same logic, shared
`sig_returns_validate_shape`). The lesson generalizes: any per-impl-item
context in a syn visitor needs the impl-item hook, not the item hook.

**First-contact yield (507 real files):** 1 verified TP / 0 FP —
riir-games `PetAiConfig`, the whole-struct orphan behind the C2 class:
extracted (riir-ai Issue 589's "thread them through" arc) for a consumer
constructor pattern that never materialized (zero `PetAiConfig` references
in riir-mmorpg-examples), `melee_reach` 0 reads anywhere, the other six
fields read only by the `> 0.0` sanity test. Same precision profile as
Plan 124's A (1 TP / 511 files). The struct stays (deletion is the owning
lane's call — the report is suggest-only); the finding is the record.

**C1 stays open** (orphaned-by-optimization needs git HISTORY — a reader
that vanished — a review-time/sweep-time heuristic, not a per-compile
scan; the intake row carries the shape).

## Issue 91 T1.5 — the per-attempt ring: `--fix-compile` attempt sequences to `.heal/fixseq/` (2026-09-12)

The instrumentation prerequisite both remaining rustc_errors-side tasks
blocked on, landed the same day as the T4/T8 emission halves (the same
class: emission-first, analysis-when-data-exists).

**Why:** T1's mining verdict — the trajectory kv records per-FAMILY aggregated
counters, NOT per-attempt sequences; the fix-compile side had ZERO recorded
trajectories. T2's oscillation detector (error A → fix → error B → fix →
error A = saddle-circling) and Issue 093's per-run strategy posterior both
need the ORDERED attempt sequence, which no shipped surface held. One
instrumentation, two kernel consumers (katgpt-rs 593 SaddleEscapeGate + 592).

**What:** `AttemptRecord { seq, code, span_hash, strategy_id, outcome,
errors }` on `FixCompileReport`, pushed at ALL five loop outcome sites (kept /
no-progress revert / the two io reverts / span-drift revert — the `applied` +
`reverted` Vecs lose the interleaved order; the ring keeps it).
`span_hash` = blake3(`"file:line"`) first 16 hex — stable across runs and
machines; the driver's canonical path resolution feeds it, so symlink forms
(/tmp vs /private/tmp) cannot fork the identity. `evolve::dump_fixseq`
writes one `run-<ts>.jsonl` per write-mode run into `<repo>/.heal/fixseq/`
(the `.heal/misses/` sibling; idempotent README; the dump_misses law —
warnings never gate, attempt-less runs write nothing). Review mode makes no
attempts and writes no file, by construction.

**E2E (live, this session):** a fresh /tmp crate with the E0502 borrow shape
→ `e0502-deref-removal` kept, `errors [1,0]`, exactly one ring row + the
README; the clean re-run wrote no second file.

Validation: lib 1223/1223 @ default (+3: span-hash stability/discrimination,
ring serde round-trip, dump ordered-jsonl + README-once + attempt-less
no-op), bin lane clippy clean, live e2e above. T2 remains open on
ACCUMULATION (real fix-compile runs to replay); T3 stands (analysis-only,
no data needed).

## Issue 089 T4+T8 — the evidence-emission halves: band-mass snapshots + per-rule bench rows (2026-09-12)

Both remaining Issue 089 tasks were blocked on EVIDENCE that only future
runs accumulate — but until this landing, nothing accumulated it: neither
the band-mass snapshot writer nor the per-rule bench emission existed.
Their emission halves are now live; T4/T8 stay open only on ACCUMULATION
(time + future generations), with the clock started 2026-09-12.

**T4's half — `frontier_snapshots.jsonl`:** every `--frontier-report` run
appends the just-measured band-mass to the COMMITTED append-only
`.benchmarks/frontier_snapshots.jsonl` (the score-history law: the committed
file is the projection). State-change dedup: an unchanged store at the same
generation appends NOTHING (ts-only differences are not rows) — one row per
measurable state, not one per report run. The `generation` field is the
FRONTIER (max generation ever run in the cwd, NOT the latest lane): lanes
interleave (a v1 rerun landed between the v8 run and the first snapshot —
latest-lane semantics would have recorded a spurious 8→1→8 oscillation on
the T4 x-axis, caught live in this session), so a new row means "a new
generation EXISTS" — the boundary the correlation samples. Rows carry:
ts/sha (the store discriminator — different repos' stores share the file,
no machine paths committed), generation frontier, population/seen/
band_count/band_mass/saturated, and the T5 per-feed split. Best-effort by
law: a failed append prints one stderr line and never fails the report.
First row: gen-8 frontier, band-mass 5.6%, saturated 2 (`use_self` 172,
`nan-unsafe-sort-comparator` 133), feeds all-organic 18/18. Dedup validated
live on the immediate re-run ("unchanged since the last row — not
appended"). The ≥3-generations GO evidence clock is RUNNING; the gate
itself stays unwired until the band-mass ↔ next-generation yield
correlation is measurable on the file.

**T8's half — `rule_outcomes` on every bench row:** the α grid-fit blocker
was that `score_history.jsonl` carried AGGREGATE heal rates per run —
nothing could be replayed per candidate. Every row now carries per-rule
`fixtures/resolved/persist/broken/created/edits/shaped`, attribution by the
T7 `shaped_half_counts` law: single-target fixtures only (a ran fixture
whose `vocab_before` is exactly one lint); multi-target composites count in
the aggregate axes, never here — the count prints loud per run ("N
multi-target fixture(s) unattributed"). The `persist`/`broken` fork is the
T4 triage vocabulary: `broken` = `FixtureOutcome::parses` false (the FULL
output-ok signal — syn-parse ∧ oracle-ran ∧ compiles), `persist` = output
ok but the target still fires. `edits` is the log-length proxy the R(n)
tie-break consumes. Same additive serde law as `ood`/`strata`/`shaped`
(instrumentation, not scored; the Warm-tier `ScoreRunRow` mirror drops it
— the schema-identity test's exceptions list extended to three). First
live row (#98, v1 lane): 4 rules attributed — `deref_addrof` 1/1,
`filter_next` 1/1, `map_unwrap_or` 2 fixtures 1 resolved + 1 PERSIST
(cross-checked against the console persist map: "map_unwrap_or x1"),
`needless_return` 1/1 (edits 2); 24 multi-target skipped. The α fit itself
stays blocked until generations of per-rule rows accumulate.

**En-route (DRY):** `git_sha` + `local_iso_timestamp` (+ private
`civil_from_days`) moved UNGATED from `score_bench::report` to
`frontier_report` (the snapshot writer needs both without the bench
feature; the bench re-exports them so every `sb::report::*` call site is
stable) — the moved `civil_from_days` also carries the module-level
`cast_possible_truncation` allow it used to inherit from report.rs's
module-level block.

Validation: lib 1220/1220 @ default (+3 snapshot tests), 1452/1452 @
score_bench (+2 per-rule tests), `generation_v8_freeze` e2e green, clippy
clean on lib (both feature states) + the full `cargo-heal` bin lane; live

## Issue 089 T7 — the shaped 0.5 verdict: generation 8 + the Elo-tie / Beta-half-count feeds (2026-09-12)

The optional third-track task, landed as a full generation. "Target cleared
∧ new diags introduced" is now a FIRST-CLASS verdict — priced 0.5 (half win)
in the bench, represented as a TIE in Elo and a HALF-COUNT (+0.5 r AND +0.5
f) in the Beta feed — with its own append-only score-bench generation.

**The creation mechanism (why the shapes exist at all):** `manual_map`'s
span-preserving rewrite splices the Some-arm body VERBATIM into a BORN
closure (`match o { Some(v) => Some(f(v)), None => None }` → `o.map(|v|
f(v))`) — the closure expression did not exist pre-fix, and the born shape
fires lints OUTSIDE `FIXABLE_LINTS` (VERIFY-only / pedantic), so the bounded
fixpoint cannot dissolve them; they SURVIVE as `created`. Anti-precedent
honored: v7's `gen7-flat-nrl-format` WAS a created-chain until Plan 097 T1's
universal `*__elem` splice dissolved it — the v8 freeze confirms the splice
class creates NOTHING today (the `gen8-splice-nrl` atom measured empty and
is excluded ON RECORD, with `gen8-birth-method` (`|v| v.len()`) and
`gen8-birth-traitmethod` (`|v| v.to_string()`) — inherent/trait method calls
do not trip `redundant_closure_for_method_calls` in the bench configuration).

**Generation v8** (`specs_v8` / `generation_v8`, `--score-bench --generation
8`): 7 authored atoms, freeze-adjudicated 2026-09-12 — 4 ADMITTED (all
closure-birth: `fncall`/`pathcall` birth `redundant_closure`; `clone` births
`map_clone` — measured beat the claimed `redundant_closure_for_method_calls`,
the oracle wins both directions; `identity` (`Some(v) => Some(v)` →
`o.map(|v| v)`) births BOTH `map_identity` AND `single_option_map`, and its
freeze label carries TWO targets — `manual_map` + `needless_match`, the
outer rewrite SUBSUMING the inner fix in one pass), 3 EXCLUDED as
dissolved shapes. Freeze e2e (`tests/generation_v8_freeze.rs`, the v7
convention + two NEW fences): the INNOCENCE fence (claimed-created lints
must NOT fire pre-heal — a created lint that already fires is a persist
mislabeled as creation) and the SHAPE gate (heal must clear the target AND
leave the created set non-empty; a dissolved atom is EXCLUDED with the
reason, never silently kept — SHAPE-NEGATIVE is a first-class freeze
verdict). Always-on gates in `generations.rs`: parse/single-target,
claim-innocence coherence, cargo-less chain-truth (all admitted atoms = 1
pass), the closure-birth `.map(|` textual canary (a future `manual_map`
change that simplifies the splice reds BEFORE any oracle run), and the
freeze-hole check over BOTH record tables (`FROZEN_LABELS_V8` + the new
`V8_CREATED` measured-created record, drift-gated by the freeze re-run).

**Scoring** (`score_bench`): `FixtureOutcome::shaped_verdict()` — 1.0 clean
clear, [`SHAPED_VERDICT`] = 0.5 target-cleared-with-new-diags, 0.0 otherwise
(broken output re-scores 0 by the existing after_verdict contract);
`BenchScore { n_shaped, shaped_credit, shaped_rate, shaped_half_counts }`;
`HistoryRecord.shaped` (the additive serde law — old rows read `None`, the
Warm-tier mirror drops it, SVG/saturation ignore it). Attribution law:
half_counts credit SINGLE-TARGET fixtures only — the identity atom's
`needless_match` resolution is deliberately NOT credited (subsumed by the
outer rewrite, not fixed by its proposer — crediting it would be
mis-attribution; the single-target law prevents this by construction).
Gen-8 admission is SHAPE non-vacuity (`n_shaped ≥ 1`), deliberately NOT the
M5 heal_rate comparison — every v8 target clears by construction, so the
plain gate would refuse the generation for measuring exactly what it exists
to measure. First live run (row #97, 2026-09-12 — the citation read #98 until a
2026-09-12 static re-read of `score_history.jsonl` corrected it; #98 is the
later gen-1 v1 rerun, the one carrying the first `rule_outcomes`): 4/4
shaped, **shaped_rate 50.0% vs heal_rate 100.0%**, created 5 lints across 4 atoms, half_counts
`manual_map`×3; the run report prints the per-atom shaped table with
drift-check against `V8_CREATED`.

**The rating feeds** (the task's second half): `elo::{update_pair_scored,
EloTable::play_scored}` — the tie representation, delegating to the
katgpt-core `update_scored` f64 primitive (substrate-first: it already
existed with draw tests; ties at equal ratings are bit-exact no-ops, the
s=1/0 endpoints are bit-identical with `update_pair`, zero-sum throughout —
pinned by 4 new tests). `frontier_report::{shaped_half_rows,
render_shaped_half_rows}` — the "Beta (half-count)" fold: each shaped
verdict adds +0.5 r AND +0.5 f, p̂ drifts toward 0.5; a rule whose only
evidence is shaped sits AT the band edge (exactly 0.500, never above — the
admission-band-ceiling-by-construction property, pinned by test). Wired
into `--frontier-report` via a plain-serde read of the latest gen-8 jsonl
row (no feature dep; EMPTY-loud when v8 has never run). The LCB/admission
math stays on the store's INTEGER feed — doubling counts to fit u32 would
fake Beta concentration (Beta(1+2r+s, 1+2f+s) ≠ Beta(1+r+s/2, 1+f+s/2));
stated in the section footer, the report-first law. Live first read:
`manual_map` r 0→1.5, f 0→1.5, p̂_folded 0.500 — the store has no organic
`manual_map` row, so the fold's band-edge property is on live display.

Validation: lib 1447/1447 @ score_bench (14 new) + 1217/1217 @ default (6

## Issue 089 T6 — the stratified score-bench read + the D-formula decline (2026-09-12)

Split verdict on the difficulty-proxy task: the closed-form D is DECLINED on
the record (both readings insufficient — mining-time D has no per-rule data

restate the n column), while the stratified-read half LANDED and paid for
itself on its first run.

The stratified read (`score_bench::{provenance_class, ProvenanceStratum,
stratify}`): every clippy-lane bench run's heal rate split by fixture
provenance class — `repo` (`repo@sha` families, organic mined), `authored`
(`authored-composite:*`), `construction` (the generated ladders — the same
word the pair vocabulary uses), `other` (fail-closed catch-all). The fixture
join REUSES the ood mining join (`ood_set_family`): v6's frozen bench rows
 carry `construction:gen6:…` metadata, but their ids live on the raw span
table with the real `repo@sha` provenance — the strata classify v6 as REPO
(guarded by test; without the join the v6 ladder would have read
construction). Printed after every clippy-lane bench + persisted additively
on the jsonl row (`HistoryRecord.strata`, the ood law: instrumentation, not
scored — SVG + saturation ignore it, the Warm-tier `ScoreRunRow` mirror
drops it, old rows deserialize as `None`). The gen-4/5 lanes write no
strata (single-class ladders — a one-row stratum would restate the
aggregate).

**First measurements (live, 2026-09-12):** v1's 96.2% aggregate is
authored-dominated — authored 98.0% (27 fixtures, 51 findings, 50 resolved)
vs repo 50.0% (8 fixtures but only 2 findings — 6 are clean/decline spans).
The v6 all-repo ladder reads 95.2% (17 spans, 21 findings, 20 resolved).
So the healer holds ~95% on real-mined material at depth (v6) and ~98% on
authored composites; v1's tiny repo surface is sample-noise territory (2
findings). The per-CLASS trend across generations is now measurable — every
bench row is generation-tagged, which is exactly what the T5 outcome-feed
per-batch blocker lacks.

## Issue 089 T5 — provenance weighting: the priced pair namespace + the enforced rating fence (2026-09-12)

The learnability-frontier instrument gained its provenance axis (the
TaskPilot/FrogNano +2.06-organic-vs-+0.00-injected effect, made measurable at
the feeds that exist today). Four coordinated halves:

1. **The vocabulary + weights** (`src/frontier_pairs.rs`, with the pair
   types): `PROVENANCE_ORGANIC` (feature-churn mined — no miner ships yet,
   the vocabulary lands first so the day one lands its rows are priced
   correctly), `SYNTHETIC_PAIR_WEIGHT = 0.05` (ε — near-zero per the paper,
   NOT zero: construction truth is fence-verified and bootstraps pools with
   no organic evidence), `provenance_weight()` (unknown tags → 0.0
   fail-closed). The module is UNGATED since this landing — the type half
   was always dependency-free (the 09-10 E0433 fix already cfg'd the corpus
   half); the any() gate was the transitional shape. `frontier_report`
   (ungated) consumes the vocabulary from every feature build.
2. **The fence, load-bearing** (`traj_store::rate_pairs`): only
   `construction` rows feed the BT fit. The PairRowDoc contract has said
   "any other provenance must never feed a rating" since Issue 072 —
   vacuous while every row was construction. Now enforced: non-construction
   rows are excluded + counted loud. The semantic: organic rows are
   curriculum-priced 1.0 precisely because they are OBSERVED, and observed
   wins are never rating evidence (the healer must not grade its own
   behavior — the non-circularity law).
3. **The `--frontier-report` tail**: the pair-namespace provenance section
   (count/share/weight/weighted per class; EMPTY-loud when no pair rows —
   both live stores honestly show 0) + the outcome-feed split
   (`{code}:{strategy}` keys = synthetic/generated-case vs every other key
   = organic/real-repo; band-mass measured PER FEED — what T4's admission
   gate will consume; a band living only in the synthetic feed is a
   curriculum artifact). Live measurements: riir-ai 21 organic/0 synthetic
   (0.0% band-mass), this repo 18 organic/0 synthetic (5.6%) — the band
   mass is all-organic on both stores.
4. **The honest blocker, stated in the report tail**: per-BATCH causal yield
   (the paper's effect size) needs generation/batch tags on rows the store
   deliberately does not carry (construction rows are byte-deterministic,
   no timestamps; learn rows are cumulative counters) — the T2 snapshot
   precedent. The split is per-FEED health, never presented as the
   curriculum effect.

The latent-only lane (`cargo test --lib --no-default-features --features
latent_retrieval`) compiled three draft test modules whose bodies need the
matcher AND the clippy+perf fixture state: 17 tests panicked at
`LatentMatcher: no domains enabled`. Found by the 2026-09-10 each-feature
rot-gate sweep; compile half fixed same day, runtime half tracked here.

The fix (23e051bc): all three modules (`draft::latent_matcher::tests`,
`draft::headroom_probe::tests`, `draft::retrieval_eval::tests`) now gate on
`all(test, latent_retrieval, clippy_lints, rust_perf)` — the exact predicate
`retrieval_eval`'s `cross_domain_agreement_rate_report` already carried
in-file, and the state the fixture set + regression floors are calibrated
on (blended floors sit ABOVE clippy-only precision; `per_domain` rows are
positional 0=clippy/1=perf). The issue's sketched `any(single-domain)` gate
would have been WRONG: the tests assert `DomainId::Clippy` rows and the
perf seed (`overlay_replaces_the_covered_domain_and_keeps_the_rest`), so a
`latent+sec`-style lane would still fail them post-gate — the matcher
builds with sec, then the clippy-row asserts panic. clippy+perf is what
the tests actually need, which was the issue's own governing phrase.

Validated: latent-only 232p/17f → 230p/0f (two passing tests also drop
from THIS lane — `mutate_shape_keeps_embedded_tokens` (pure) and
`router_spectral_poc_report` (router report) — both still run in every
clippy+perf+latent lane); calibration lane (default+latent) 1301p/0f with
24 of the modules' tests present by name (5+6+13; `kernel_mutation_*`
stays out until kernel_heal joins); clippy clean at both feature sets.
Standing caveat, out of scope: the latent-only lane carries ~15 pre-existing
domain-less dead-code warnings (unused `index_domain` macro, unused
`HealDomain` imports, `mut`-not-needed on `router_domains`) — the lane has
no clippy guard, which is the same premise this issue existed to close.
No guard-layer count moves: the guard's lanes (5b default, 5c all-features)
