### Boundary contract — full text (was AGENTS.md lines 5–22)

## Boundary contract — read `BOUNDARY.md` first

[`BOUNDARY.md`](BOUNDARY.md) is the authoritative per-repo contract: what this
repo **owns**, what it **does not own** (with the correct home for each), the
crate-granular **allowlist** of what it may depend on, links to the cross-repo
rules' one canonical home, and the **drift ledger** of known gaps. On any
conflict with prose in this file, BOUNDARY.md wins.

- **Domain test:** is this a **developer tool** (clippy healing, codegen) with zero game-domain coupling in the default build? NO → it belongs in another repo; file there.
- **Read it before** adding any dep, crate, module, System impl, or vocabulary
  type — and before assuming a concern is yours to implement.
- **Enforcement** is not prose: `../riir-ai/scripts/ci_boundary_contract.sh`
  fails on an undeclared cross-repo dep, on a drift row without its open issue,
  and on a contract row that no longer matches the measured graph. Run boundary
  checks VIA the `boundary-guard` skill, not as ad-hoc greps.
- **Found a violation?** File the issue FIRST (`.issues/NNN_boundary_*.md`), add
  the drift row, then fix. Closing the issue removes the row in the same commit.

### Why this is a separate repo — full text (was AGENTS.md lines 3613–3637)

## Why this is a separate repo (not in riir-ai)

The code healer borrows the **drafter+pruner+corpus pattern** from
`riir-games-quest/quest_grammar` (TernaryDraftModel + SealQuestCorpus +
ConstraintPruner), but has **zero game-domain coupling**:

- No dependency on `riir-games*`, `riir-game-sdk`, or any game crate —
  from ANY feature combination
- No dependency on `riir-chain`; `riir-neuron-db` only transitive (via
  `riir-rag` under the opt-in `latent_retrieval` feature)
- Default build: only public dep is `katgpt-core` (ConstraintPruner trait
  + ternary SIMD matvec + `pick_domain` for kernel_opt's expert router,
  katgpt-rs Plan 558). Two opt-in feature-gated arms consume non-game sibling
  crates where reimplementation would duplicate whole substrates:
  `ternary_inference` → `riir-engine` + `riir-gpu` (Bench 010 inference
  arm); `latent_retrieval` → `riir-rag` (Plan 005 retrieval substrate,
  `cargo heal --suggest`)
- The `TernaryDraftModel` pattern is reimplemented locally (~200 LOC), not
  imported cross-workspace

Putting it in riir-ai would violate the domain boundary: riir-ai is for **game
runtime + engine**, not developer tools. The prior rejection of extracting
riir-games from riir-ai (Proposal 017 era) was correct because riir-games has
heavy bidirectional coupling with riir-engine. Code healing has no such
coupling — it's a clean, self-contained developer tool.
### CI enforcement — full text (was AGENTS.md lines 3740–3758)

### CI enforcement (2026-09-02, katgpt-rs Issue 701 R2 self-apply)

`.github/workflows/rust.yml` now runs `scripts/ci_feature_guard.sh` — the
same guard a developer runs, not a CI-only subset. Triggers are deliberately
narrow (the workspace spending-limit convention): **weekly on `develop`**
(the rot check — the default branch IS the working branch here), pushes to
`main`, and `workflow_dispatch`. The `standalone` job pins the
escaping-path-dep set (`scripts/standalone_dep_gate.sh`: 9 entries across 3
siblings — katgpt-rs public; riir-ai + riir-neuron-db private via
`SIBLING_REPOS_TOKEN`, hard-erroring when the token is absent, the riir-chain
Issue 028 expiry-alarm pattern). Runner notes: the toolchain installs from
rust-toolchain.toml (never @stable — the single-toolchain-across-8-repos pin
is deliberate); the Tier-2 `docker build --check` agreement degrades
deterministically in CI via a dead `DOCKER_HOST` (daemon + registry from
shared runner IPs is a flake factory — local runs own the live-oracle
coverage); the guard's layer-5c wedge budget is raised to 7200 s for the
4-core runner. First scheduled runs are the cost measurement: budget ~300 min
(30-feature `--each-feature` layer + the all-features GPU tree, floating
sibling HEADs).
### Documentation Shape — full text (was AGENTS.md lines 3810–3840)

## Documentation Shape

This repo ships a **11-folder numbered `.docs/` book** (opened 2026-08-11,
Issue 007; the 11th folder was added for the Plan 001 domains), matching the `riir-ai/.docs/` / `riir-neuron-db/.docs/` /
`riir-game-sdk/.docs/` format: numbered folders for sort order, unnumbered
`.md` files inside, each folder has a `README.md` index with a purpose
blockquote + file table + "See also" cross-refs.

| Folder | Scope |
|---|---|
| `01_orientation/` | Crate role, sibling layout, boundary rationale, multi-domain architecture (Plan 001), build commands, numbering |
| `02_corpus/` | L0 rule distillation: `Corpus<D>` (generic) + BLAKE3 commitment + per-domain seed corpora |
| `03_drafter/` | L1 ternary SIMD matvec: `TernaryDrafter` (generic over `E: HealEntry`) + BLAKE3 `embedder` + Plan 005 latent retrieval (`RuleIndex`/`DomainRouter`/`LatentMatcher`, `--suggest` MVP, Bench 018 GOAT G1–G4) |
| `04_pruner/` | L2 syn validator: `RustAnalyzerPruner` + `ValidationResult` + honesty contract |
| `05_clippy_verify/` | clippy lint resolution: `ClippyVerifier` (opt-in `clippy_verify`) |
| `06_ruliology/` | L3 Pareto-front: `RuliologySearch` + `pareto_front` + `ast_delta_size` (opt-in) |
| `07_examples/` | The 8 in-tree examples (`heal_demo`, `perf_heal_demo`, `perf_bench_demo`, `kernel_heal_demo`, `clippy_verify_demo`, `ruliology_search_demo`, `self_evolve_real_world_demo`, `stage2_tuning_demo`) + the `cargo-heal` bin (Plan 005 `--suggest` CLI) |
| `08_benchmarks/` | GOAT gate methodology + measured results |
| `09_lessons/` | Canonical patterns: borrow-without-dep, modelless-first, freeze/thaw, honest POC caveats, sigmoid-not-softmax |
| `10_self_evolve/` | Issue 004 + Issue 008: latent-first self-evolution loop (`HealPipeline` + `LatentFixMemory` + `LatentSkillEvolution`, opt-in `self_evolve`; G1–G7 ALL PASS) |
| `11_domains/` | **Plan 001 Phase 2+3**: multi-domain architecture — `rust_perf` (Phase 2) + `kernel_opt` (Phase 3, absorbs Proposal 012) |

The top-level `.docs/README.md` is the index. `README.md` (repo root) remains
the build surface (Status + Quick Start + Usage); `AGENTS.md` (this file)
remains the authoritative repo-local context.

For `.docs/`: files inside numbered folders have **no number prefix**.
Filenames are bare slugs (e.g. `crate_role.md`). The folder number provides
sort order; the filename provides identity. Add a new doc by dropping
`slug.md` in the right group folder and adding one line to that folder's
`README.md` index table.
### Numbering Discipline + Research-note shape — full text (was AGENTS.md lines 3842–3879)

## Numbering Discipline

Issue, plan, doc, benchmark, and research numbers are **monotonic and never
reused**. Before creating a new `.issues/` file, read `.issues/.highwater`, use
`value + 1`, write back. Same for `.plans/`, `.docs/`, `.benchmarks/`,
`.research/`, and `.distill/` (the distill-program rolling resume state —
edit-in-place per batch, NOT one file per batch; see
`.distill/001_mining_queue_snapshot.md` and the pointer section in
`.agents/skills/riir-clippy/SKILL.md`).

**One counter per directory, enforced (Issue 069 T3, decided 2026-09-05 —
option (a)).** Every author reads the directory's `.highwater` and writes
`value + 1` back in the same commit; a renumber consumes its target exactly
like a fresh allocation (the riir-ai Bench 847 rule). The discipline is
checkable, not remembered: katgpt-rs `scripts/numbering_drift_sweep.py` reds
on tracked duplicates above this repo's pinned count and on a `.highwater`
below its directory max. Note `numbering_gate.py` (the per-push half) is
katgpt-rs-scoped — its floors file is that repo's — so this repo is covered
by the sweep, not the per-push gate; the standing fix for a collision is
renumber + citation rewrite per katgpt-rs Issue 724 T2, never a silent reuse.

### Research-note shape (convention, adopted 2026-08-16)

`.research/` notes are **born-complete distillation records**, not task
trackers — no `- [ ]` checkboxes (pending work lives in `.issues/`, the
SKILL.md mining queue, or the plan the note feeds). Two header rules:

1. Every new note carries a `**Status:**` line (not `**Outcome:**` — legacy
   notes using it are grandfathered) from a small vocabulary: `RECORD`
   (batch landed, closed) · `DISTILLED — pending owner decision` (has an
   actionable unimplemented delta) · `NEGATIVE` (measured refutation).
2. A note whose delta gets filed/implemented later gets a one-line status
   update pointing at the issue/commit — the note itself stays a record.

Rationale: 36/58 historical notes have no Status line, which is benign only
because they are closed records; the two genuinely-pending notes (053, 058)
DO carry explicit Status lines. The vocabulary makes that distinction
machine-skimmable for future sessions.

## 2026-09-12 — Issue 092 T1: the GW corpus-alignment PoC, measured and closed (defend-wrong NEGATIVE)

The 371/594 fusion idea (align two healer rule-corpora's similarity spaces
with GW → cross-domain correspondence map for dedup + fix-transfer) ran its
defend-wrong PoC and lost, cleanly and at matched review budget.

**Instrument:** katgpt-rs `b09f1368` exposed the GW coupling publicly
(`gw_coupling` — same deterministic multi-start solve, returns the winning
coupling matrix instead of only its scalar loss; identity-correspondence +
bit-determinism unit tests). The PoC harness is `examples/gw_corpus_poc.rs`
behind opt-in `gw_corpus` (measurement-only; no heal-path, no router).

**Protocol:** clippy_lints (49) × rust_perf (126) = 6,174 pairs. Arm (a) GW:
trigram-cosine distance over `buggy_code`+`fixed_code` ONLY (names withheld —
sharing the baseline's lexical signal would be circular), perf split even/odd
into 63-halves (GW_MAX=64), two solves unioned. Arm (b): token Jaccard over
rule identifiers (today's name/convention dedup as a ranking). Arm (c): stride
base rate. Ground truth: 180 hand-labeled pair reads (ALL top-60 of each arm +
60 stride pairs) against criteria fixed before labeling.

**Result:** GW precision@60 = 0.017 = the base rate (no signal); name/keyword
0.083 = 5× base rate. GW's strongest couplings (full-column masses) were
structural artifacts (`collapsible_else_if`×`powi-vs-powf`); the one
GW-exclusive TRUE (`manual_slice_fill`×`retain-inplace`) is a data point, not
a win. Robust to any single label flip. The planned known-negative class was
EMPTY (no perf `context_notes` names any of the 49 clippy lints — the
"Distinct from" refs are all within-domain).

**Mechanism:** surface-trigram distance structure is not fix-shape structure;
and this test bed's true correspondences are name-visible by construction
(both corpora name rules after the same Rust API surface — the disjoint-
vocabulary regime where structure-only alignment could win does not exist
between these two corpora). Reopen trigger recorded in the issue: a semantic
fix-shape embedding (AST/transform fingerprints) or a disjoint-vocabulary
corpus pair (clippy × docker).

Full record + 180-label appendix: `.benchmarks/083_gw_corpus_alignment_poc.md`.
Issue 092 closed (T2–T4 never fired). Research note 166 §A verdict updated.

## 2026-09-12 — Issue 093 T1: the per-run strategy-posterior PoC, measured WIN (defend-wrong)

The 373/592 fusion idea (a per-run `NonergodicFilter` over strategy
 generators — 545 §4's "file-level posterior, nonergodic upgrade of the
router", at strategy level) ran its defend-wrong PoC and WON all three
scenarios.

**Instrument:** the katgpt-rs Plan 592 kernel consumed directly —
`katgpt-micro-belief` becomes an 11th escaping path dep (opt-in, feature-
forwarded `nonergodic_belief`; already transitive via katgpt-core defaults —
the row is the direct gate, BOUNDARY + standalone pin updated same commit).
Harness: `examples/nonergodic_driver_poc.rs` behind opt-in `nonergodic_poc`
(measurement-only). Arm B is the REAL `shape_conditional_order` over a seeded
TrajStore — the actual shipped competitor, not a simulation of it.

**Protocol:** 1,200 paired file-runs per cell (240 files × 5 seeds); 10 REAL
playbook strategies (E0597's 6-strategy menu is where ordering bites);
outcomes are BLAKE3 draws from frozen (regime × difficulty) tables keyed by
(site, strategy, context-hash) — same bytes + same context → same outcome
(the tried-set guarantee), context change → fresh draw (the compiler's
verdict on a re-proposed edit depends on the current file). Scenarios:
aligned / stale (regime-swapped store — the world changed under the store) /
cold. Fourth arm D composes store+filter (λ_t = t/(t+1)) — the T2 production
shape.

**Result:** C (filter) resolved 41.7% vs A (min-delta) 35.2% and B 36.7%
aligned / 34.3% stale (B drops BELOW A under a stale store); wasted-attempt
54.8% vs 58.6/56.5; McNemar 160/82 vs A (z≈5.0), 146/86 vs B aligned (z≈3.9).
Misspec pass (±20% on the filter's tables, world unchanged): edge holds
entirely — the load-bearing property is the regime winner-SPREAD, not exact
values. C is store-independent by construction (identical rows across
scenarios — the paired-design sanity check).

**The harness bug worth remembering:** the first draft's revive rule fired on
posterior flip alone — 356 revives, 0 helped, provably: a frozen-context
retry is the same bytes against the same file, so its outcome CANNOT change.
Fixed before the recorded run: revive requires the suppression CONTEXT to
have moved too (another fix landed in between), which is also the faithful
model of the real driver (a changed diagnostic at the site is a NEW
TriedKey, not a revive). Post-fix: 57/50 net-positive. D under a stale store
shows the cost of composing with a lying prior (78/137 revives, 38.2% —
the λ-schedule needs a stale-detection gate, recorded as T2 design space).

**Honest bounds:** C's model family matches the world generator family by
construction (regimes ARE the generators; misspec covers parameters, not
family); the toy store is deliberately sparse (2 events/shape — B's aligned
win over A is NOT significant at this density, 138/120 p≈0.24, and NO claim
is made about the shipped ordering at real densities). T2's GOAT on the real
1%-fail surface is the family-error test.

**T2 unlocked** (T1 win + Issue 91 T1.5 ring landed `795ddc4c`): opt-in
wiring at the `rustc_errors` driver ordering seam, uniform or store-seeded
priors per run, context-scoped revives, GOAT = resolved-rate-at-equal-budget
on the real corpus via the G6/G7 floor A/B harness.

Full record: `.benchmarks/084_nonergodic_driver_poc.md`. Research note 166 §B
verdict updated.

## 2026-09-12 — Issue 094: trajectory covariability-class mining PoC, measured and closed (defend-wrong NEGATIVE)

The Research-309 consumer hypothesis — the sliceTCA drift-class share per
rule predicts which corpus rules needed re-mining (proposer revision/guard
after landing) — ran its defend-wrong PoC and lost to the activity
confound. The failure is the STORE SCHEMA's, mostly, and that distinction
is recorded below.

**Instrument:** `examples/tca_covariability_poc.rs` behind the existing
`latent_retrieval` feature (no new feature key — `slice_tca` is default-on
in katgpt-core since katgpt-rs Plan 596 / Bench 714, so no forwarding needed).
Stores read via `/tmp` MIRRORS only (sibling `.heal` trees are read-only to
a session; the mirror guarantees zero writes upstream). Ground truth = the
2026-09-12 re-mined(33)/stable(27) label snapshot dug from
`.distill/001` §Post-mining intake P1–P19 mapped to proposer-fix commits
(clippy lane snake_case keys, rust_perf kebab — the store's exact
spellings; dogfood commits and the mechanical b83230ee emitter migration
excluded from labels).

**Protocol:** tensor X[rule, day, shape-bucket] over the 10 store-bearing
repos — 12,557 rows → 4,496 cells after filters (rustc_errors `:` keys,
Withdrawn tier, 8,060 no-timestamp game-sdk rows). Axes: [35 rules] ×
[18 days] × [32 FNV-1a buckets]; cell = ln(1 + success + fail) mass.
Classifier path only (`covariability_shares`, 3 SVDs per probe — the
issue's "may suffice" arm). Per-rule score: leave-one-rule-out
ΔEVR_time. Eval: exact Mann-Whitney AUC over labeled rules carrying mass
(30 of 60; 23 re-mined, 7 stable), pre-registered PASS rule = beat every
baseline.

**Result:** AUC(S_tca, r=4) = 0.497 — chance (robustness: r=2 → 0.438,
r=8 → 0.469). Baselines: total log-mass 0.689 (best — the activity
confound: rules that fire get revised), fail-share 0.559, day-entropy
0.099 (stable rules spread MORE evenly — the inverse of the naive drift
expectation), majority 0.5. Global covariability shares saturate
(entity 0.990 / time 0.994 / episode 0.985): one hot rule
(`uninlined_format_args`, log-mass 1879 of ~2900) dominates every
unfolding's top-R spectrum, so per-rule LOO deltas are scale-driven, not
class-driven. FAIL per the pre-registered rule.

**Mechanism (honest bounds):** the store keeps CUMULATIVE counters per
(rule, shape) with only the LAST verdict's timestamp — the session axis
collapses to "day of last fire", so time-slicing measures shape-churn-day-
clustering, not within-shape drift; 30/60 labels carry zero mass
(survivorship: quiet stable rules are absent from the store, and the
stable rules that DO fire look like re-mined ones). The drift hypothesis
is NOT refuted for event-level data — it is untestable at this schema.
Reopen triggers: (a) per-event trajectory rows persisted store-side (the
fixseq ring is the precedent shape) giving a true session axis; (b)
balanced per-rule outcome labels (score-bench `rule_outcomes` rows are the
per-rule precedent).

Full numbers: the harness output (this commit's run) + the issue file's
git history. Issue 094 closed (the FAIL branch of its own task 4).
riir-neuron-db Research 309's consumer-surface line got a status delta (healer surface:
measured negative; neuron-db Plan 329 unaffected — different data,
event-level telemetry is its design center).

(a no-surface null is not a measured negative). Issue 093 stays open as the

**En route (pre-existing, Windows-only):** `orphan_report::GitCli::new`
compared canonicalized scan paths against git's root WITHOUT canonicalizing
the root — on Windows `canonicalize()` yields the verbatim `\?\C:\…` form
while `rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns `C:/…`, every pathspec dropped,
the whole history leg blind; `real_git_e2e_orphan_lifecycle` failed 3/3
deterministic on this box (it landed green from macOS, where canonicalize
adds no prefix — the L132 symlink comment shows the class was half-seen).

"validated-on-one-OS" lesson again — the sibling-session's 1247/0 was true
on macOS and silently false on Windows.

## 2026-09-12 — Issue 098: the rule-corpus cross-OOO axis, measured PASS + wired (absorption candidates found)

**Issue 098 RESOLVED** ([Bench 086](.benchmarks/086_rule_corpus_cross_ooo_axis.md);
the Research 552 §F2 fusion from katgpt-rs Issue 759 / riir-ai Research 378).
The absorption/splitting audit aimed at this repo's own rule bank: rules =
units, each rule's oracle-labeled triggering spans = its MEI set (ALL of
them — a binary oracle has no graded activation, so the bank is RAGGED and
the free `ooo_score`/`cross_ooo` kernels compose into a hand-built
`BankAudit` for `greedy_curate`; `audit_bank_into`'s uniform top-K does not
apply).

**Metric evolution (the katgpt-rs Bench 758 metric-granularity law, observed live):**
plain TF-cosine over `RustOpBigramTokenizer` tokens was the control and was
REJECTED — it let the generic scaffold swamp the rare op signatures on
micro-span rules and pinned three pairs at exactly 0.500 (the tie
signature). The tokenizer's own design doc names the law ("ubiquitous runs
earn near-zero IDF... rare ones earn high IDF and do the separating") —

### 2026-09-15 addendum — Issue 108 T3+T4: the full measurement, the schedule amendment, and the honest negative

T3 ran same-day (the oracle's stub-crate runs are ~1 call/s — the full
37-arm pass took ~3 minutes, not the estimated hour; the "measurement-heavy"
deferral evaporated on contact). Two harness amendments landed mid-T3,
both discovered by the first full run:

1. **Presence-ranked schedule.** The issue's "top-20 by heal rate" cannot
   fill on the v1 set: the T8 `rule_outcomes` read attributes
   single-target fixtures only, and the set is multi-target-dominated
   (4 solo rows on 35 ran fixtures). Ranking by solo heal rate schedules
   4 rules and misses exactly where composed necessity lives. The
   amendment: rank by findings PRESENCE (Σ fixtures where the rule is in
   `vocab_before`) — every at-risk finding counted, multi-target
   included; solo columns stay the T8 read.
2. **Verdict ladder Δ-first.** The first ladder checked `solo_resolved == 0`
   before Δ — a multi-target-only rule with a nonzero Δ would have read
   "NO-EVIDENCE". Reordered: Δ != 0 → LOAD-BEARING unconditionally (13 of
   the 18 rows would have been mislabeled — including `identity_op`,
   solo=0, Δdisabled=−6).

**The measurement ([Bench 092](.benchmarks/092_component_necessity_flip_rate.md)):**
18 targets, 36 arms + baseline + planted no-op; canaries green both sides
(the no-op arm's per-fixture fingerprint byte-identical to baseline —
cross-arm determinism proven). **18/18 LOAD-BEARING, zero decoratives.**
The three findings: (1) no dead weight among the busiest rules — the
decorative class exists in theory but not in this population (name-presence
scoring: a finding survives unless SOMETHING dissolves its shape, and no
two FIXABLE proposers claim overlapping territory on this set); (2) solo
rate massively understates composed importance (`needless_return` solo=1
vs Δ=−17; `identity_op` has NO solo row at all — per-rule pruning off the
T8 read alone would misrank both); (3) Δswap ≈ Δdis everywhere —
co-occurrence donors are shape-DISJOINT (rules co-fire on the same file,
not the same span), so a real donor-flip study wants Issue 098's cross-OOO
absorption pairs as the donor pool, not co-occurrence argmax.

Demote/repair decisions: NONE warranted (empty decorative list). Issue 108
RESOLVED and removed per the noise rule; Bench 092 + this entry are the
record.

## 2026-09-15 — Intake class P22: `--platform-audit`, the platform-dead_code decl-vs-use cfg lattice

The 2026-09-14 P22 intake row recorded the class: items declared
UNCONDITIONALLY whose every use sits inside a platform-gated context —
5 specimens across 2 repos in 2 days (katgpt-rs `NEON_U8` fixed
`ea4c2873`; zed `KEYCHAIN_SERVICE` + 3 more fixed `a4f70e64a7`), ALL
caught by x86_64/Windows gate runs that no CI lane owns. The class is
invisible to any single-platform CI matrix: the gate is ON where CI
compiles, so the use exists there, while every other platform compiles
the item to dead weight nobody warns about. rustc's `dead_code` cannot
fire either — one gated use silences it on every platform it compiles.

The intake's verdict held: SYNTAX-CORPUS OUT (detection needs cfg-lattice
reasoning, not a fix-space) — the home is an audit instrument, not a
proposer. `cargo heal --platform-audit [PATHS…]` (`src/platform_audit.rs`,
ungated, syn + std, zero new deps) is that instrument:

- **Lattice**: per tracked module-level decl (`const`/`static`/`fn`/
  `use`), intersect the platform atoms every use site's cfg GUARANTEES
  (mod-stack union; multiple cfg attrs AND — union; `any()` arms
  intersect; `not()` proves no positive platform; `feature` atoms DROP —
  the cfg-audit family owns that class). An atom in the intersection the
  declaration's own cfg lacks is the witness: the item is dead on every
  platform that atom excludes.
- **The two-map import split** (the landing's own design catch): a
  `use a::b::C` resolves on every platform the IMPORT compiles, so the
  import's own path is a real use of the SOURCE const — but it says
  nothing about the LOCAL binding. An ungated import whose only code
  mentions are gated is exactly the zed `ProcessStatus` specimen and must
  stay flaggable. Code mentions and import references therefore tally
  into separate maps: `use`-decls read only code evidence; value decls
  read the union. A gated import condemns its source through RENAMES
  only (`use a::C as D` separates the names); a same-name pair reads as
  ambiguity and is skipped — the conservative direction, pinned by test.
- **Contract**: report-first, gates nothing; exit 0 on every real scan,
  REFUSES exit 1 on an empty/unparsable scan (the frontier-report law);
  the two scope hints (unscanned roots + downstream consumers) ride the
  output like config-audit/orphan-report.

Validated against the real historical evidence (git-archive extractions
— zero writes to the sibling):

- katgpt-pruners @ `ea4c2873^` → **exactly 1 finding = NEON_U8**
  (simd.rs:27, dead outside `target_arch = "aarch64"`) — 1 TP / 0 FP
  over 268 files / 5950 decls.
- katgpt-pruners @ `ea4c2873` (the fix) → 0 findings — the gate on the
  decl is detected.
- Self-scan → 1 row (`ECHO_DAEMON`, l4_daemon.rs:273, test-only): a
  TRUE-in-shape instance the module's own
  `#![cfg_attr(not(unix), allow(dead_code))]` already acknowledges —
  the adjudication path working as designed, no fix warranted.
- riir-chain src → 0 findings / 0 FP (177 files); riir-dao crates → 0
  (23 files). Refusal + exit-0 contract live-verified on a nonexistent
  path (exit 1) and a clean scan (exit 0).

Gates: 20 fixture tests (the pre/post-fix specimen pair, `any`/`not`/
`all` semantics, the two-map import split, rename tracking, ambiguity
skip, test-only marker, pub marker, empty-scan refusal); lib 1482/1482;
clippy `-D warnings` clean on lib + the cargo-heal bin; the
`standalone_modes_are_never_bare` contract test carries the new row.
Five mechanical clippy findings on the landing (must_use × 2,
doc_markdown × 3) were healer-first'd — `cargo heal --fix --write
--verify` took the one in-corpus finding class (`vec-with-capacity` in
config_audit, the shared-helper exposure); the rest were manual (out of
corpus, the documented fallback).

The P22 intake row is ticked DONE in the same commit; the 2026-09-14
OPPONENT WATCH row's checkbox is ticked to match its already-recorded
content (hygiene — the record was complete, the box simply never moved).

### v3, same day — P24 (b)+(d) consumed (the mod-row lattice + the macro arg scan) — P24 COMPLETE

The last two intake items landed together; **P24 is now fully consumed.**

**(b) The `ModRowLattice`**: every external `mod x;` row is indexed with
its full nesting context (the declaring file's root `#![cfg]` ∪ inline
mod nesting ∪ the row's own cfg), resolved to its child file by the
standard rustc 2018 path rules (root files — `lib.rs`/`main.rs`/`build.rs`
+ direct `.rs` children of `bin`/`tests`/`examples`/`benches` — and
`mod.rs` resolve children in their own directory; every other file in a
directory named after its stem; inline `mod a { mod b; }` nests
`<base>/a/`), then the child's UNIQUE incoming row folds its atoms (plus
the parent's own effective atoms, transitively — memoized recursion)
into the child's root ctx, exactly like the v2 file fold: both the decl
and the use side, by construction. `audit_sources` restructured into
parse → lattice → walk phases (all trees stay alive for the lattice —
the v2 (c) walk prune is what keeps that memory bounded). Divergences,
all in the no-fold direction: `#[path]`-carrying rows, children absent
from the scanned set, fn-local `mod x;` statements, and files whose
incoming rows disagree (the lib.rs + main.rs ambiguity — skip, keep
own). A wrong root classification can only mis-resolve into the
no-fold direction.

**(d) The macro arg scan**: the format family
(`format!`/`println!`/`write!`/`panic!`/tracing/`bail`/`ensure`…)
counts inline `{ident}` captures in its string literals (doubled `{{`
and positional `{0}` excluded), and BOTH it and the `assert*`/`matches`
family count ident tokens in their EXPRESSION args — path prefixes
(`a::` in `a::b`) and macro names (`foo!`) skipped so a multi-segment
path counts once on its last segment, the `visit_path` rule. Never
expansion; overcounting is the documented safe direction (a phantom use
can only suppress a flag, never raise one). The assert-family leg was
born from the v3 sweep's own FPs: chaind's `stream_type::SIGNALING` +
`BrowserNodeState` native test uses sit inside `assert_eq!`/`assert!`

lesson hitting this walk's own front door: name-global masquerades
against `data/mining_v3/files/rust-lang__rust/*.rs`, a GITIGNORED
rustc-snapshot corpus (`git check-ignore` → `.gitignore:149`) no repo
owns. The repair moves the whole file-set derivation, not the
classifier: `read_sources` (config_audit.rs — shared by
`--config-audit` / `--orphan-report` / `--platform-audit`) is now
`read_sources_walk`, deriving the set per directory root from
`git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- '*.rs'` when
the root is inside a repository.

**Semantics, chosen over the intake's literal "tracked-only" wording:**
the goal is gitignore-exclusion, not tracked-purity. `--cached --others
--exclude-standard` is tracked + untracked-NON-IGNORED — a fresh WIP
file stays in the scan (a report that silently misses un-added files
would be a regression the sweep would only notice at the worst moment),
and a TRACKED file matching a later-added ignore rule stays too (git
cannot retroactively ignore the index — `tbi.rs` fixture). Nested
foreign checkouts fall out for free: untracked nested repos list as a
single directory entry that matches no `*.rs` pathspec, submodule
gitlinks likewise — v2's symlink/`.git`-file walk prune survives only
in the fallback. Explicitly named FILES and entirely-ignored directory
ROOTS are scanned anyway (caller intent wins — the ignored-dir root
falls back to the filesystem walk for that root, recorded as `Plain`).
Roots outside a repo (fixtures, /tmp probes, git absent from PATH)
keep the v2 filesystem walk. Every consuming report now prints a
`walk:` line (the new `WalkMode`: `Git`/`Plain`/`Mixed` with root
counts) directly under its population line — before the blind branch,
so even a refusal shows the walk mode. The distinction is never
silent.

## 2026-09-15 — Issue 109: the orphan-report FP specimens repaired (foreign-literal attribution + generic serde bridges)

The issue was filed as instrument intake — two FP classes the 2026-09-15
quiet-repo sweep measured, with candidate repairs sketched. This landing is
the instrument pass it was filed for.

**(a) Per-file foreign-literal attribution (`config_audit::FileScope`).**
Within one Rust file, a bare `Name { … }` literal resolves ONLY to a type
declared in that file, an explicit import, or a glob — never to a
sibling module's same-named struct. The candidate net (and the wire pass)
matched type NAMES file-globally, so bevy's `Node { … }` in a file importing
`use bevy::prelude::*` masqueraded as construction evidence for the LOCAL
serde `Node` declared in riir-shader-graph — 4 stillborn rows, zero true
findings — and, in a serde fn, would have FALSELY CLEARED the local
struct's rows. The repair skips provably-foreign literals in both
directions (candidate sites AND wire-type membership). Precedence mirrors
rustc at file granularity: own decl > explicit import > glob; foreign =
explicit foreign import, or foreign-glob-with-no-local-decl/import.

**The over-suppression the first cut measured before its rescue:** a
WORKSPACE scan sees `use editor_core::types::XRow` from a sibling crate
whose declaration IS in the scanned set — syntactically indistinguishable
from `bevy_ui` without crate-name knowledge. The first cut read those as
foreign and the editor lost 207 candidates + all 26 C1 rows (for the wrong
reason — the bridge repair hadn't even fired). The rescue:
`scan_local_crate_roots` — the scan's dash-normalized path components
(`crates/editor-core/…` → `editor_core`) read workspace-sibling imports as
LOCAL. Sound in the single-crate scan posture too: a cross-crate import of
a scanned-declared name can only appear in files outside the declaring
crate, which such a scan does not carry.

**(b) Generic serde bridges (`orphan_report` wire pass).**
`fn row_to_mapping<T: serde::Serialize>(row: &T)` — the bridge fn has NO
struct literal (the serialized value is the generic param) and its callers
have NO serde call, so fn-scoped co-occurrence is not merely missed, it is
INAPPLICABLE. The repair detects bridges (Serialize-bounded param in the
param list OR a where clause — `save_t`'s shape — plus a serde `to_*` call
on the VALUE param typed over it; the param-mention guard keeps
unrelated-concrete serializers out) and harvests the concrete types at
call sites by turbofish: the call's own `save_t::<CraftRow>(m)` and
arg-position `row_to_mapping(&Repo::<CraftRow>::get(..))`. Stillborn rows
on bridge types count as `bridge-cleared` (the measured-FP posture of
`wire_cleared`); ORPHANED rows keep their history evidence but render
**wire-dto weak** — the receiver consumes the serialized field, so the
in-repo read loss is evidence, not a death verdict. Bridge types
deliberately do NOT seed the wire-const/cleared sites loop: per-field const
classification stays direct-serde-fn evidence, bridge clearance is
struct-level in the classifier (the conflation was caught by its own
fixture before landing — the seeding made a bridge type's plain literal
site read as `wire-cleared` instead of `bridge-cleared`).

**Real-tree validation.** riir-shader: the 4 specimen rows → 0 stillborn
(candidates 164 → 154, the 10 foreign-literal candidates left the net; the
1 silent row unchanged). seal-game-editor: 26 C1 rows → 22 strong + 4
wire-dto weak — exactly the Cluster B four (`CraftRow`,
`ComposeTemplateRow`, `StoneStepRow`, `StoneOptCostRow`) via the
`row_to_mapping`/`save_t` turbofish call sites; `ItemRow`/`DropTierRow`
stay strong C1 (no detectable bridge on their lane — the editor's own
issue-157 adjudication owns them; that repo is read-only here). Regression
canaries exact-match the P25 baselines: self 0 orphaned / 11 stillborn /
370 files; riir-ai 0/70/2897; katgpt-rs 0/14; riir-dao's pinned
`[wire-const] EpochSummary.provenance_verified` SURVIVES; riir-chain 0/0.

**Gates.** 9 new fixtures (4 candidate-side: foreign glob, explicit foreign
import, workspace-sibling rescue, in-crate import; 5 wire-side: the
foreign-literal-in-serde-fn false-clear negative, the turbofish bridge
(param list + where clause), the unrelated-concrete negative, and the two
end-to-end classifier shapes — bridge-cleared stillborn + wire-dto-weak
orphaned). lib 1515/1515; clippy clean on all touched code (the healer was
invoked first for the raw-string-hash class — silent, its documented
divergence; manual for the rest). Landing also fixed a pre-existing dead
`let base` in the P25 walk test (test-build warning, `_base`).

**The lesson worth keeping (twice in one landing):** the fixture class
where a raw string opens `r#"` and terminates `";` does not fail to parse —
it SWALLOWS the following tests into string content until the next real
`"#`, silently unregistering them and splicing one test's asserts into
another's thread. Three fixtures cost an hour of phantom debugging
("compiled but not registered", panic attributed to a test whose source
has no such assert) before the mechanism was visible. When tests vanish
from `--list` while their source sits at module level, suspect the raw
string terminators first.

The third specimen class contributed to the 109 ledger (the previous
session's DumpEntity `Serialize`-wire-contract rows, consumed by the
substrate's matching authority dump in ANOTHER repo) is NOT repaired by
either mechanism — readers outside the scanned set are the documented
scope limit; the downstream-consumers hint names the repos. Issue 109
resolved; file removed per the noise-reduction rule.

## 2026-09-16 — the Issue-109 re-sight closed: scan-global struct field sets (the foreign-glob + local-glob shape)

Found by the session's own housekeeping sweep: re-running `--orphan-report`
over riir-shader returned **4 stillborn rows at `ui.rs:269-274` on bevy's
`Node` fields** — the exact FP family the 2026-09-15 Issue-109 repair had
measured at 0. Not a fixture regression: the bevy 0.17.3 → 0.19 migration
(`d8c938b`, 16:56 +0700 the same day) rewrote the showcase UI literals, and
the file carries BOTH `use bevy::prelude::*` (foreign glob) AND
`use riir_shader_core::prelude::*` (workspace-sibling glob) — the shape
`FileScope::literal_is_foreign` documents as UNDECIDABLE ("a foreign glob
alongside a local glob reads local — the conservative direction"). The
literal read local, the scan-global name match found the serde-backed
`riir-shader-graph::Node`, and the 4 rows re-entered through the documented
hole. The existing fixture family only covered the foreign-glob-ONLY file.

**The closure is the compile argument, not a better import heuristic:**
`collect_struct_field_sets` — scan-global field sets for every TOP-LEVEL
`struct` declaration, unioned across same-named decls (mod-nested decls
excluded, consistent with `FileScope::of`'s top-level rule — a bare literal
in another file can never name one without a path). A literal naming a
field that NO local same-named decl has PROVABLY cannot be any of them: a
construction of the local type must compile against its real fields, so
the mismatch is a foreign type masquerading under the same name.
`literal_is_field_mismatch` is applied in BOTH evidence consumers — the
serde-literal candidate net (`StructLitCollector`) and the orphan wire
pass (`WireVisitor`: neither construction sites nor wire-type membership,
mirroring the specimen-A early return). The no-reject direction is
conservative: no local decl of the name, an all-unnamed (tuple) literal,
or a field present on SOME same-named decl → evidence stays.

**Measured:** riir-shader 4 stillborn → 0, candidates 170 → 160 (the 10
foreign-literal fields dropped); every recorded canary byte-identical —
self 0 orphaned / 11 stillborn / 373 files, riir-ai 70 stillborn, riir-chain
0/0 + the 2 P26 marker rows, riir-deployer + riir-auth marker rows, dao's
pinned `[wire-const] provenance_verified`, riir-dapps all-zero, and
riir-mmorpg-examples' 4 orphaned rows still the adjudicated
`DumpEntity.{h,hp,k,s}` NO-ACTION family. +3 fixtures (the re-sight shape,
the union-rescue control, the wire false-clearance negative) → 39/39
orphan + 41/41 config-audit, **lib 1534/1534**, clippy `-D warnings` clean
(the one `must_use_candidate` on the now-`pub` `field_member_name` was
healer-first — silent, its documented divergence; manual `#[must_use]`).
Footers of both reports name the new skip direction.

## 2026-09-16 — P31: the fn-A/fn-B inter-procedural wire-clearance (orphan-report; the riir-kat queue-writer intake)

The 2026-09-16 quiet-repo audit batch's orphan intake, at 16-row
concentration in one protocol leaf: riir-kat's intent DTOs
(`VoteIntent`/`StakeIntent`/`UnstakeIntent`/`ClaimRequest` — version +
reference + `queued_unix` fields) are literal-constructed in FLOW fns whose
own bodies contain no `serde_json::to_*` path call (`json!` + `Value`'s
`.to_string()` are not serde paths), and serialized by SIBLING queue-writer
fns (`queue_vote_intent`: `serde_json::to_string(intent)`). Fn-scoped
co-occurrence cannot join the two by construction — the documented
"built-in-fn-A/serialized-in-fn-B stays flagged, the conservative
direction" divergence, at concentration.

**Fix, two arms:** (1) `serialized_concrete_param_types` — a fn whose body
serde-serializes one of its own CONCRETE-typed params (per-param mention
check; generic `T: Serialize` params stay `is_generic_serde_bridge`'s lane)
contributes that param's type to `direct_wire_types`, so the caller's
literal sites clear/wire-const exactly as if they sat inside the serde fn.
(2) Macro token-stream scanning — the queue-writer's serde call sits INSIDE
`writeln!(...)`, which syn's visitor does not descend:
`token_stream_serde_to_mentions` matches the exact `serde_json::`/`serde_yaml::`
to_* path at token level (ident equality, two `:` puncts, a following
parenthesis group; recursive through nested groups) and checks the argument
group for the param ident — hooked into BOTH `block_has_serde_call`'s and
`block_serializes_param`'s finders via `visit_expr_macro`/`visit_item_macro`.
This also widens bridge detection to macro-wrapped serde calls (same class,
the correct direction) and makes `in_serde_fn` fire for literal-in-fn +
serde-in-macro shapes.

**Measured:** riir-kat 16 stillborn → **4** (the remaining four are
`ProposalView`×3 + `PoolView`×1 — the Deserialize-side schema types, the
recorded under-reported-consumer standing class), wire-cleared 8 → 19,
wire-const 0 → 1 (an all-const-site field rendered at the weak class —
honest). Self 11 → **8** stillborn (377 files — the batch-148 file growth
plus three fn-A/fn-B shapes of the fixstats lane now clearing). Every other
recorded canary holds byte-identical: **riir-ai 70 stillborn unchanged**,
dao 0/0 + the pinned `[wire-const]` row, riir-mmorpg-examples' 4 orphaned
`DumpEntity` NO-ACTION family, riir-chain 0/0 + 9 silent. +2 fixtures (the
queue-writer positive — a const-PATH field value is not a literal; the
per-param negative — a fn serializing an unrelated value while merely
receiving a param of the type does not clear it) → **lib 1566/1566**,
clippy clean. Footer + `WireConsumption.cleared` doc updated — the
"built-in-fn-A stays flagged" clause replaced by the sibling-fn link. Global
binary rebuilt from this tree with the release feature set and installed
over the symlink target (verified: riir-kat 4/19 through the global).
Remaining conservative gaps, on record: turbofish'd `to_string::<T>(..)` at
token level, and method-shaped serializers (`self.to_json()`), and the
Deserialize-side `from_slice::<T>` schema classes — the last is the standing
under-reported-consumer class, NOT cleared (a deserialized field's local
reads may still be owed).

## 2026-09-18 — Issue 124: the ops-plane ladder re-pointed at the riir-llm leaf

The Issue-051/106 extraction leaf landed its first consumer (dao) the same
morning; this closes the second: `src/groq.rs` + `src/cf_workers_ai.rs` no
longer carry their own copies of anything the leaf owns.

**The seam, stated** (it is the whole design decision): the leaf owns WIRE
MECHANICS — URL shapes (EndpointConf now carries base URLs; the leaf's
`Wire::url` appends the route — the URL shape had already diverged once
between the dao and clippy copies), body builders (`chat_body_for`,
wire-aware model placement: OpenAI carries the model in the body, CF is
model-free), response parsers (`Leg::parse` / `parse_cf_result`), failure
classification (`OaiError` is now an ALIAS of `riir_llm::LlmFailure` —
one vocabulary, four variants incl. the Auth stop-class), both timeout
ceilings, and bearer hygiene (`post_chat_on` scrubs; the three clippy-side
scrub/auth/debug tests retired into the leaf's). riir-clippy keeps POLICY:
the windowed-disable `LlmRouter` (a rate-limited leg disables for the
whole WINDOW — the leaf's ladder is stateless per attempt; that asymmetry
is deliberate, not duplication), FreeTierStats + the `providers.*`
ledger/dashboard contract (new `auth_errors` key, additive), `avoided_usd`
pricing, the USD cap + reserve-then-reconcile, the GraphQL usage meter
(the leaf speaks chat-completions, not GraphQL), the regate harness.

**Measured facts moved with their code**: the qwen3 `/no_think` suffix,
the GLM-4/GLM-5 thinking-switch split, the both-schema CF result walk,
and the eleven body/parse tests — now leaf tests. The clippy side keeps
ONE wiring test per client (base-URL + wire + model-free-CF-body + the
GLM-thinking env dispatch) and re-pins the overflow prefix end-to-end
through the leaf parse.

**Behavior changes, deliberate**: (1) a 401/403 from a free leg is now
STOP-class (surfaced labeled, counted in `auth_errors`) — previously it
wore the Transport costume and silently shifted the window onto the PAID
CF leg; (2) an empty-content non-length OpenAI response falls through
instead of "serving" an empty string; (3) `OaiGen` drops the dead
diagnostics (`total_tokens`, the quota-header fields — only the live-smoke
print ever read them); (4) `groq_first` no longer names `dep:ureq` (the
leaf's transport IS the ureq now — surface shrink, 12 escaping deps across
five siblings, `transport::Agent` re-exported so no consumer needs its own
ureq dep for the type).

**Live validation**: groq live smoke PASS through the new path
(`post_chat_on` + `Leg::parse`, 3eb31e5 leaf) — the qwen body rides the
leaf's builder byte-compatibly. The CF body is byte-identical to the
measured shape by construction (same fields, same order, still
model-free), so no CF call was burned.

**The shared-worktree note**: `src/kat_footer.rs` carries a SIBLING
session's in-flight D1 grant-bar removal (owner call 2026-09-18) — this
change's one kat_footer fix (the `format_push_string` lint that pre-dated
it, af5e5e87) was SUPERSEDED by that rework (the lint site was deleted
with the function) and reverted here; the file belongs to that session's
commit. `groq_first`-only also never compiled its live router smoke
(missing `cf_workers_ai` cfg — latent since the test landed, surfaced by
making the posture real); gated now.

## 2026-09-22 — Issue 129: the cargo-heal scoop-bucket 0.1.4 manifest 404 (URL pointed at the v0.1.3 tag)

`bucket/cargo-heal.json` in `gist-rs/scoop-bucket` declared
`"version": "0.1.4"` but its download URL fetched from the **v0.1.3** tag —
no `cargo-heal-v0.1.4-*` asset exists there, so every scoop install/upgrade
of cargo-heal 0.1.4 on Windows 404'd since the 0.1.4 bump. The `hash` field
was already correct; only the URL's tag was stale — exactly the shape a
hand-edit produces (version string bumped, URL string missed).

**Fix + verification** (same day, scoop-bucket `9f70496`): one-line URL tag
`v0.1.3` → `v0.1.4`, verified END-TO-END — `curl -sL` the fixed URL →
sha256 byte-identical to the manifest's hash AND to the v0.1.4 release's
own `SHA256SUMS` row for the windows zip.

**Prevention (the lane note)**: `release.yml` (Plan 105) owns tap/bucket
PRs on `v*` tags, but the 0.1.4 bucket row landed as a manual commit — a
hand path with no mechanical coupling between the version string and the
URL tag. Prefer the release.yml bucket-PR lane for every bump; when
hand-editing is unavoidable, copy BOTH `url` and `hash` from the freshly
cut release's assets (never retype the tag), and curl the URL once before
pushing — a 404 in a bucket manifest is a broken install for every Windows
user, not a docs nit.

Found during the katgpt-rs Plan 606 (riir-reflex Phase 2) T2.3 session (previously carried as
"noted, not mine" in the Phase-2 handoff); the reflex-side record is
riir-reflex `e5dcfc9`. Issue file removed per the noise-reduction rule —
this row is the durable record.
